```md
### Servicing logs (CBS and DISM)

`clean.cbs-logs` | Standard | Tier B | method files | reversible: none

*Removes old servicing log files and their compressed archives (admin). The three newest files are kept.*

Deletes old CBS and DISM log files and their .cab archives. The newest three files are kept so recent servicing problems can still be diagnosed, and logs in use are skipped. Deleted logs cannot be restored.

**Folders:**

- `%SystemRoot%\Logs\CBS`
- `%SystemRoot%\Logs\DISM`

**Filters:** older than 72 h; only *.log, *.cab; keeps the newest 3.

### Component store cleanup (DISM)

`clean.component-store` | Advanced | Tier A | method dism | reversible: none

*Runs DISM StartComponentCleanup to remove superseded update components (admin). Can take several minutes.*

Uses Repair-WindowsImage -StartComponentCleanup, the supported way to shrink the WinSxS component store. It removes superseded component versions that Windows would also clean on its own schedule. iG Windows Tuner never deletes inside WinSxS directly. Updates installed in the last 30 days stay uninstallable.

**Side effects:** Older superseded update versions can no longer be restored.

**Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/clean-up-the-winsxs-folder>

### Component store cleanup with /ResetBase

`clean.component-store-resetbase` | Expert | Tier A | method dism | reversible: none

*DISM cleanup with ResetBase: frees the most space but makes all installed updates permanent (no uninstall).*

Runs StartComponentCleanup with ResetBase, which removes every superseded component version. All currently installed updates become permanent and cannot be uninstalled. Use it only on a stable system you do not need to roll back.

**Side effects:** Installed updates can no longer be uninstalled.

**Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/clean-up-the-winsxs-folder>

### Delivery Optimization cache

`clean.delivery-optimization` | Standard | Tier A | method deliveryOptimization | reversible: none

*Empties the Delivery Optimization cache with Windows' own cmdlet (needs admin). Updates still download normally.*

Runs Delete-DeliveryOptimizationCache, the supported way to empty the cache that Windows Update and Store downloads use. Windows refills it only as needed. Nothing to revert: the cache is rebuilt automatically.

**Side effects:** Content in the cache is downloaded again if it is needed later.

**Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/deliveryoptimization/delete-deliveryoptimizationcache>

### Old driver packages

`clean.driver-store` | Expert | Tier A | method driverStore | reversible: none

*Removes older third-party driver versions not used by any device, via pnputil without /force (admin).*

Finds third-party driver packages that have a newer version of the same package installed and are not bound to any present device. It removes them with pnputil /delete-driver without /force, so Windows refuses anything in use. Rolling a device back to a removed version then needs the old installer.

**Side effects:** Device Manager 'Roll Back Driver' can no longer return to the removed versions.

**Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devtest/pnputil-command-syntax>

### Crash dumps (minidumps and live kernel reports)

`clean.memory-dumps` | Advanced | Tier B | method files | reversible: none

*Deletes old crash dumps but keeps the newest one (admin). Keep all dumps while you investigate a BSoD.*

Deletes minidumps and live kernel reports created after blue screens and driver hangs, keeping the newest file for diagnosis. Full MEMORY.DMP is removed by Windows in Settings > Temporary files. Deleted dumps cannot be restored.

**Side effects:** Older crash dumps are no longer available for analysis.

**Folders:**

- `%SystemRoot%\Minidump`
- `%SystemRoot%\LiveKernelReports`

**Filters:** older than 24 h; only *.dmp; keeps the newest 1.

### Recycle Bin (all drives)

`clean.recycle-bin` | Standard | Tier B | method recycleBin | reversible: none

*Empties your Recycle Bin on every fixed drive. Restore anything you still need first; this cannot be undone.*

Empties the current user's Recycle Bin on each fixed drive with Clear-RecycleBin. Files in the Recycle Bin are permanently deleted. Storage Sense can do this automatically for items older than 30 days instead.

**Side effects:** Deleted files can no longer be restored from the Recycle Bin.

### Thumbnail cache

`clean.thumbnail-cache` | Standard | Tier B | method files | reversible: none

*Deletes Explorer thumbnail caches so they are rebuilt. Files Explorer has open are skipped; icons are untouched.*

Deletes the thumbcache_*.db files that Explorer uses for picture and video previews. Use it when thumbnails look wrong or the cache has grown large. Explorer rebuilds thumbnails as you browse, so folders with many pictures load slower once. The icon cache is never touched.

**Side effects:** Thumbnails are regenerated the next time you open those folders.

**Folders:**

- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer`

**Filters:** only thumbcache_*.db; never iconcache*.

### User temporary files

`clean.user.temp` | Standard | Tier A | method files | reversible: none

*Deletes files older than 24 hours from your user temp folder. Files that are in use are skipped.*

Removes leftover files in %TEMP% that installers and apps forgot to delete. Only files older than 24 hours (by both creation and last-write time) are touched, files in use are skipped, and empty subfolders are removed. Deleted files cannot be restored; apps recreate what they need.

**Side effects:** An app that was paused mid-task for over a day may need to restart that task.

**Folders:**

- `%TEMP%`

**Filters:** older than 24 h.

**Sources:** <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/free-up-drive-space-in-windows-85529ccb-c365-490d-b548-831022bc9b32>

### Windows Error Reporting (system reports)

`clean.wer.system` | Standard | Tier B | method files | reversible: none

*Removes system-wide crash and hang reports (needs admin). Keep them if you are troubleshooting a crash.*

Deletes the machine-wide Windows Error Reporting archive, queue and temp folders under ProgramData. These reports can be large after app or driver crashes. Deleted reports cannot be restored.

**Side effects:** Unsent system crash reports are discarded.

**Folders:**

- `%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\WER\ReportArchive`
- `%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\WER\ReportQueue`
- `%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\WER\Temp`

**Filters:** older than 24 h.

### Windows Error Reporting (your reports)

`clean.wer.user` | Standard | Tier B | method files | reversible: none

*Removes queued and archived crash reports for your account. Keep them if you are troubleshooting a crash.*

Deletes your Windows Error Reporting archive and queue (crash and hang reports already sent or waiting). They are only useful while troubleshooting; Reliability Monitor keeps its summary. Deleted reports cannot be restored.

**Side effects:** Unsent crash reports for your account are discarded.

**Folders:**

- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\WER\ReportArchive`
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\WER\ReportQueue`
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\WER\Temp`

**Filters:** older than 24 h.

### Windows temporary files

`clean.windows.temp` | Standard | Tier A | method files | reversible: none

*Deletes files older than 24 hours from C:\Windows\Temp (needs admin). Files in use are skipped.*

Removes old files from the system temp folder used by Windows services and installers. Only files older than 24 hours are deleted and locked files are skipped. Deleted files cannot be restored; Windows recreates what it needs.

**Folders:**

- `%SystemRoot%\Temp`

**Filters:** older than 24 h.

**Sources:** <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/free-up-drive-space-in-windows-85529ccb-c365-490d-b548-831022bc9b32>

### Previous Windows installation (Windows.old)

`clean.windows-old` | Expert | Tier A | method guidance | reversible: full

*Shows the size of Windows.old and upgrade leftovers. Remove them in Settings to keep Windows' own rollback logic.*

Reports the size of C:\Windows.old and the upgrade staging folders. Removing them deletes your ability to go back to the previous Windows version, so iG Windows Tuner hands this to Windows itself: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > Previous Windows installation(s).

**Side effects:** Removing it (in Settings) makes the upgrade permanent.

**Folders:**

- `C:\Windows.old`
- `C:\$WINDOWS.~BT`
- `C:\$WINDOWS.~WS`

*Note:* Guidance only: use Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > Previous Windows installation(s).

**Sources:** <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/delete-your-previous-version-of-windows-f8b26680-e083-c710-b757-7567d69dbb74>

### Windows Update download cache

`clean.windows-update-cache` | Advanced | Tier A | method files | reversible: none

*Clears downloaded update files; stops and restarts Windows Update, BITS and DO (admin). Fixes stuck downloads.*

Deletes the contents of C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download, which is Microsoft's documented step for resetting stuck Windows Update downloads. The Windows Update, BITS and Delivery Optimization services are stopped first and always restarted afterwards. Pending updates download again.

**Side effects:** Updates that were already downloaded are downloaded again.

**Folders:**

- `%SystemRoot%\SoftwareDistribution\Download`

**Filters:** stops and restarts wuauserv, bits, dosvc.

**Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/installing-updates-features-roles/additional-resources-for-windows-update>

### AMD shader caches

`clean.gaming.amd-shader` | Standard | Tier B | method files | reversible: none

*Clears AMD DirectX, DXC, OpenGL and Vulkan shader caches. First game launches rebuild shaders.*

Deletes the AMD driver shader caches. Clearing them after a driver update avoids stale shaders. Games rebuild them on the next launch, which can cause brief stutter.

**Side effects:** Shaders are rebuilt on next launch; expect brief stutter the first time.

**Folders:**

- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Edge\User Data (profiles: Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache, DawnCache, DawnGraphiteCache, DawnWebGPUCache; root: ShaderCache, GrShaderCache, GraphiteDawnCache)`

### Mozilla Firefox cache

`clean.browser.firefox` | Standard | Tier B | method browserCache | reversible: none

*Clears Firefox's disk cache for every profile. Firefox must be closed. Cookies, history and passwords stay.*

Deletes the cache2, startupCache, jumpListCache and thumbnails folders in each Firefox profile under Local AppData. The real profiles (cookies, history, passwords, add-ons) live in Roaming AppData and are protected. Firefox must be closed.

**Side effects:** Pages load a little slower the first time while the cache refills.

**Folders:**

### Opera and Opera GX cache

`clean.browser.opera` | Standard | Tier B | method files | reversible: none

*Clears the Opera and Opera GX disk caches in Local AppData. Opera must be closed. Cookies and history stay.*

Deletes the Opera and Opera GX cache folders under Local AppData. Profile data (cookies, history, passwords) lives in Roaming AppData, which iG Windows Tuner protects and never cleans. Opera must be fully closed.

**Side effects:** Pages load a little slower the first time while the cache refills.

- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Opera Software\Opera GX Stable\Cache`

`clean.browser.vivaldi` | Standard | Tier B | method browserCache | reversible: none
```

`docs/DECISIONS.md`:

```md
# Decisions and deviations

Every place where the implementation deviates from the original specification, or where the specification left a choice, is recorded here with its reason and source. The rule applied throughout: **when in doubt, keep the Windows default; when documentation and the seed catalog disagree, follow the documentation.**

## Tweak catalog corrections

| # | Topic | Specification | Decision | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | MMCSS "Games" task profile (GPU Priority 8, Priority 6, Scheduling Category High, SFIO High) | Tier B, Competitive | **Rejected** (documented in `rejected.json`). Microsoft documents *GPU Priority* as "not yet used", *SFIO Priority* as "not used", and says *Priority* is "always treated as 2" when Scheduling Category is High. Only threads that register with the MMCSS "Games" task are affected at all. The only remaining effect would be Scheduling Category High (priority 23-26, meant for pro audio), which can starve system threads. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/multimedia-class-scheduler-service> |
| D2 | MMCSS SystemResponsiveness | 10; "verify handling of values < 10" | Kept at **10**. Microsoft: values not divisible by 10 are rounded down, and values below 10 or above 100 are clamped to 20. So 0 (a common recommendation) behaves like the default 20, and 10 is the lowest effective value. | same |
| D3 | "No auto-restart while signed in" (`NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers`) | Tier A, all presets | **Replaced** by the documented active-hours policy (`SetActiveHours=1`, 10:00-04:00, the 18 h maximum). Microsoft states that the policy "doesn't work exactly as per description", only applies with `AUOptions=4`, and "can result in no quality update reboots" at all, which is security-reducing. Added to the Rejected list. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/update/waas-restart> |
| D4 | "Nagle off" (`TcpAckFrequency=1`, `TCPNoDelay=1`) | Tier B, manual | Implemented as **"TCP delayed ACK off"** with `TcpAckFrequency` only (documented in KB 328890). `TCPNoDelay` as an interface registry value is not read by the Windows TCP stack (Nagle is the per-socket `TCP_NODELAY` option), so it is rejected. The hint states that UDP games (Dota 2, CS2, VALORANT, LoL) are unaffected. | <https://support.microsoft.com/kb/328890> (now <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/registry-entry-control-tcp-acknowledgment-behavior>), <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winsock/ipproto-tcp-socket-options> |
| D5 | Accessibility hotkeys (StickyKeys 506, Keyboard Response 122, ToggleKeys 58) | Fixed values | iG Windows Tuner **clears only the hotkey flag** (`0x4`) of the current value instead of writing fixed numbers. With Windows defaults the result is exactly 506/122/58, but users who rely on Sticky/Filter/Toggle Keys keep their other options. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/ns-winuser-stickykeys> (and the FILTERKEYS/TOGGLEKEYS pages) |
| D6 | Diagnostic data: `AllowTelemetry=1` plus DiagTrack disabled | One Tier A item | **Split.** `AllowTelemetry=1` (Required, the lowest level honored on Pro) stays Tier A in all presets. Disabling the DiagTrack service also stops Required data, which goes beyond Microsoft's supported configuration for Pro, so it is a separate **Tier B manual** toggle (`privacy.diagtrack-disabled`). On the target PC DiagTrack is already disabled, and iG Windows Tuner detects and reports that. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/configure-windows-diagnostic-data-in-your-organization> |
| D7 | Per-game GPU = High performance | Tier B, presets C and B | **Competitive only.** Section 10 defines Balanced as "No Tier B". It also reports NotApplicable here because only the RTX 3080 is active (UHD 770 disabled). | Specification section 10 |
| D8 | Ultimate Performance plan | Tier A | **Tier B** (still Competitive). The scheme ships with Windows (resource text "Provides ultimate performance on higher end PCs") and is duplicated with the documented `powercfg /duplicatescheme`, but Microsoft's 2018 announcement post is offline (404) and no current Microsoft page documents it. Its measured gain over High performance is small. A copy that already exists is reused, and revert deletes only a copy that iG Windows Tuner created. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options> |
| D9 | NIC "allow the computer to turn off this device" | Tier A, presets C, B, H | **Tier B, Competitive only.** The only Microsoft documentation (KB 2740020, `PnPCapabilities=24`) was written for Windows 7 and has been retired (both the English and localized URLs now redirect to a generic power-management page). NetAdapterCx drivers may ignore the value, and `Set-NetAdapterPowerManagement` does not expose the option. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/2848292/power-management-allow-the-computer-to-turn-off-th> |
| D10 | AI features off (Copilot/Recall) | Tier A, Hardened | Uses only policies Microsoft documents for **Pro**: `AllowRecallEnablement=0`, `DisableAIDataAnalysis=1`, `DisableClickToDo=1` (listed for Insider builds; may be ignored), and Paint `DisableCocreator`/`DisableGenerativeFill`/`DisableImageCreator`. **Not implemented:** `TurnOffWindowsCopilot` (deprecated, and "isn't for the new Copilot experience") and `RemoveMicrosoftCopilotApp` (Pro is not supported). Recall exists only on Copilot+ PCs, so those values have no visible effect on this hardware. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-windowsai> |
| D11 | Defender "gaming-friendly scans" | Scheduled quick scan off-hours, `ScanOnlyIfIdleEnabled`, `ScanAvgCPULoadFactor=20` | Sets `ScanOnlyIfIdleEnabled=True` and `ScanAvgCPULoadFactor=20`. **No quick-scan time is set**, because `ScanScheduleQuickScanTime` only matters when scheduled scans are configured. On consumer Pro, scans run during Automatic Maintenance (idle), which already keeps them out of matches. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/schedule-antivirus-scans> |
| D12 | SmartScreen on | "Apps and Edge" | **Repair-only.** iG Windows Tuner ensures Explorer `SmartScreenEnabled` is `Warn` (absent = Warn) and removes policy values that *disable* SmartScreen for Windows or Edge. On a default system nothing is written, so Windows Security does not show "managed by your organization". | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/virus-and-threat-protection/microsoft-defender-smartscreen/available-settings> |
| D13 | SMB signing / SMBv1 | "Verify and enforce Win11 24H2+ defaults" | The client `RequireSecuritySignature` is treated as on when absent (24H2 requires signing by default). The server value is written explicitly (1), because its absent-value behavior on Pro is not unambiguously documented. SMB1 stays disabled through the optional-feature cmdlets and is never removed. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/file-server/smb-signing-overview>, <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/whats-new/whats-new-windows-11-version-24h2> |
| D14 | Background recording off | `GameDVR_Enabled=0`, `AppCaptureEnabled=0` | Also sets `HistoricalCaptureEnabled=0` ("Record what happened"). The machine policy `AllowGameDVR` is reported as ManagedByPolicy rather than written, because the per-user Settings values keep Game Bar's other features. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-applicationmanagement#allowgamedvr> |
| D15 | Game traffic QoS "Do not use NLA" | Part of the tweak | Kept, written as REG_SZ "1". It is documented by router/VoIP vendors (for example Cisco), not by Microsoft, which is one reason the tweak is Tier B. Policies are created only for games marked `"qos": true` (Dota 2, CS2, VALORANT, LoL). | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/netqos/new-netqospolicy> |
| D16 | Global timer resolution | Tier B, "Expert only" | Implemented as an **expert** toggle (`-AcknowledgeRisk` / GUI confirmation), never in a preset. | <https://randomascii.wordpress.com/2020/10/04/windows-timer-resolution-the-great-rule-change/> |
| D17 | Kernel stack protection | Tier B, manual | Implemented with the values behind the Windows Security toggle (`Scenarios\KernelShadowStacks\Enabled`, plus `WasEnabledBy=2` only if missing). Microsoft documents the feature, not the registry value, so it stays Tier B. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/security/kernel-mode-hardware-stack-protection> |
| D18 | Memory integrity "Reset to Windows default" | - | The documented default used by Reset is **on** (memory integrity is on by default on compatible clean installs of Windows 11), so a reset can never lower security. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/enable-virtualization-based-protection-of-code-integrity> |
| D19 | Advertising ID / tips / suggestions | "Ads/suggestions off" | Uses the documented policies (`AdvertisingInfo\DisabledByGroupPolicy`, `CloudContent\DisableTailoredExperiencesWithDiagnosticData`, `AllowOnlineTips`) plus the per-user values behind the Settings toggles (ContentDeliveryManager, `Start_IrisRecommendations`). `DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures` is not used because it is Enterprise/Education only. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/manage-connections-from-windows-operating-system-components-to-microsoft-services>, <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-settings#allowonlinetips> |
| D20 | Power Throttling | "Keep Power Throttling ON" | Implemented as a Tier A **repair** item (`power.power-throttling-on`) that removes `PowerThrottlingOff` if a tool set it. Disabling Power Throttling is in the Rejected list. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/quality-of-service> |

## Presets

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | **Hardened is a strict superset of Balanced** (including PCIe ASPM off, which the seed table marked only C and B). The one exception is that the Office/Adobe ASR rules are in Block mode, replacing Balanced's Audit mode. | Section 10 defines Hardened as "Balanced plus the H items"; the ASR audit and block items are mutually exclusive. |
| P2 | Hardened uses **Quad9** DNS-over-HTTPS (Cloudflare is offered as a manual alternative). Plain-DNS fallback is off. | Quad9 blocks known malicious domains, which fits a security preset. Both are on Windows' built-in DoH list. The tweak warns that router DNS, local host names and router filtering are bypassed (the target PC uses its router, 10.10.100.254, as DNS). |
| P3 | ASR Office/Adobe rules: the Audit tweak counts an existing **Block** rule as satisfied and never downgrades it. | Never weaken an existing protection. |

## Engine and platform

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Restore points are created through the WMI class `root\default:SystemRestore` instead of `Checkpoint-Computer`. | `Checkpoint-Computer` does not exist in PowerShell 7; WMI works in both 5.1 and 7. |
| E2 | Binary registry data in snapshots is stored as **hex text**, not Base64. | Keeps the shipped code free of Base64 APIs (one of the Defender-friendliness rules) and makes snapshots human-readable. |
| E3 | Adapter advanced properties are written with `-NoRestart` (requires: reboot). | Never drop the network link mid-apply, especially over Remote Desktop. |
| E4 | Kernel DMA protection is detected with `Win32_DeviceGuard.AvailableSecurityProperties` value 3. | Querying the Kernel DMA Protection flag directly needs an undocumented native call, which would add a second P/Invoke. msinfo32 confirms it. |
| E5 | Non-elevated TPM detection uses the "Trusted Platform Module 2.0" PnP device; full readiness (`Get-Tpm`) needs elevation. | `Get-Tpm` and `Win32_Tpm` require administrator rights, and `-Report` must run read-only without elevation. |
| E6 | The CPU microcode is parsed from the 4-byte `Update Revision` format (26300 stores `2F 01 00 00` = 0x12F); the older 8-byte format (revision in the high DWORD) is also handled. | Observed on the target PC; both formats are covered by unit tests. |
| E7 | **Per-monitor DPI.** WPF hosted by `powershell.exe` is system-DPI aware and renders vector UI crisply at 100/125/150 % on the primary display. Per-monitor-V2 awareness would need an application manifest or a second P/Invoke (`SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext`), which conflicts with the "one P/Invoke" rule. Layouts were verified by rendering every page at 1.0/1.25/1.5 scale (`Show-IgwtGui -RenderTo -Scale`). | Specification section 5 vs section 9 |
| E8 | Turning a toggle **off** in the GUI reverts from the newest iG Windows Tuner snapshot if one exists; otherwise it resets to the documented Windows default. The preview says which will happen. | "Off" must restore the user's previous value, not an arbitrary one. |
| E9 | Startup Apps toggles apply immediately, with a snapshot (like Task Manager), and require elevation. | They are single, fully reversible StartupApproved values, and a snapshot is always written. Requiring admin keeps all backups in the admin-only folder. |
| E10 | A short-lived read cache (5-10 s) is used for slow queries such as `Get-MpPreference` and `powercfg /list`. It is cleared at the start of every operation and after every write, and disabled in TestMode. | A full state scan went from about 10 s to about 3 s without risking stale state. |
| E11 | Pester **5.7.1** is the documented test runner (5.x API). Pester 6.2.0 was also installed by `Install-Module -MinimumVersion 5.5.0`, but `tools\Invoke-QualityChecks.ps1` pins 5.x. | Section 14 asks for Pester 5. |
| E12 | Three PSScriptAnalyzer rules are excluded in `PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1`, with justification: `PSReviewUnusedParameter` (uniform action signature), `PSUseSingularNouns` (collection getters) and `PSUseOutputTypeCorrectly` (informational). UI-only `Update-*`/`New-*` functions carry targeted `SuppressMessage` attributes. | Section 14: "warnings fixed or justified". |
| E13 | FACEIT's support pages return HTTP 403 to automated fetches. Their content was verified through search results and press coverage; the Riot page was fetched directly. | See `docs\ANTICHEAT.md`. |

## Schema v2 and migration (2.0)

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | **The tweak tier stays in `evidence.tier`**; cleaner rules carry a top-level `tier`. Loaded tweaks get a computed `tier` property, so every item kind exposes it the same way. | The spec lists "level, tier" as fields; for tweaks the tier belongs next to the sources that justify it, and duplicating it could drift. |
| S2 | **v1 levels are derived, not guessed by hand:** expert + not anti-cheat safe = Lab, other expert = Expert, Tier B or medium/high risk = Advanced, otherwise Standard. Result: 42 Standard, 23 Advanced, 2 Expert, 1 Lab. | Deterministic and reviewable; Lab matches spec section 4 ("knowingly breaks anti-cheat or a security feature"), which describes the VBS/HVCI-off toggle. |
| S3 | **`antiCheat` is derived from `antiCheatSafe` plus the warning text** (known names: FACEIT, Riot Vanguard, Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, RICOCHET, Javelin); with no name found it would be `"unknown"`. | Keeps the documented anti-cheat impact exact instead of a generic "breaks". |
| S4 | **v1 `appliesTo.hardware` became `appliesTo.conditions`**, and the new `hardware.tags` start empty. | The v1 values (wired adapter present, Defender active, not RDP, multiple GPUs) are runtime conditions, not hardware tags. Real tags come from the hardware profile engine in phase 2; the tag vocabulary (`data\hardware\tags.json`) is defined now so validation can reject unknown tags. |
| S5 | **v1 snapshots are never rewritten.** They are upgraded in memory on read (and listed normally); the tool only writes schema 2 copies to a different folder. `data\migration\id-map.json` (empty in 2.0) handles future id renames. | Backups are the user's safety net; changing them in place could break the only way back. A real 1.0 snapshot is a test fixture and is reverted by the suite. |
| S6 | **v1 presets became intent presets** (`include`, `exclude`, `levelCeiling: Advanced`, `antiCheatPolicy: safeOnly`, `gaming: true`); the in-memory `tweaks` list is `include` minus `exclude`. Preset hints were written by hand after the migration. | Spec section 10. The engine, CLI and GUI keep using one resolved member list, which phase 2 extends with overlays. |
| S7 | **Data files are written with `ConvertTo-IgwtJson`**, not `ConvertTo-Json`. | Windows PowerShell 5.1 escapes `<`, `>` and `'` (so `<absent>` becomes `<absent>`), has a depth limit and produces irregular indentation. The custom writer is ASCII-only and round-trips every data file (tested). |
| S8 | **Expert and Lab gates are unchanged for now:** both need `-AcknowledgeRisk` or the GUI confirmation, as in 1.0. The one-time acknowledgement, mandatory restore point, typed confirmation and red banner (spec section 4) come with the GUI mode switch in phase 10. | The gates belong in the GUI restructure; changing them twice would be churn. |
| S9 | **No git commit for phase 1.** git is still not installed and installing it is not allowed on this PC; the checkpoint is recorded in `PROGRESS.md`. | Development safety rule. |
| S10 | **Cleaner rule tier:** A when the rule cites a vendor source, B for well-known cache locations without one. | Same meaning as the tweak tiers: documented vs. situational. |

## Action handlers (2.0)

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | **No `bcd` handler.** BCD stays read-only (the inspector may run `bcdedit /enum` in a later phase); there are no BCD writes, not even for Lab items. | The v1 invariant and the project's scope notes; `tests\Safety.Tests.ps1` keeps enforcing it. This deviates from spec section 3/11 on purpose. |
| A2 | **No `fileAssociation` writer.** Windows protects per-user default apps with the UserChoice hash, and the only programmatic method (the DefaultAssociationsConfiguration policy) applies to domain-joined PCs only. A read-only `check` (`checker: DefaultApp`) shows the current default app and points to Settings > Apps > Default apps. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-applicationdefaults>; writing hash-protected values would be a bypass. |
| A3 | **ASR exclusions are deferred to the ASR Center (phase 5).** The existing `asrRule` handler keeps its modes. Resolved in R3/R4. | Exclusions weaken a rule for specific paths and belong next to the per-rule gamer-impact notes and audit data. |
| A4 | **Registry-backed types are composites** (`storageSense`, `wufbPolicy`, `deviceInterrupt`, `serviceSet`): they expand into the existing registry/service parts and reuse their snapshot and restore code; the expansion always comes from the catalog (and the devices present now), never from the snapshot file. | One proven primitive for exact types, absent values and created keys. |
| A5 | **`deviceInterrupt`** only targets present PCI Display, Net and USB host controllers, sets MSI values only where the driver declares MSI support, refuses USB host controllers when Windows boots from USB, needs `requires: reboot` and level Expert or Lab, and has no "reset to default" (the driver INF sets the defaults; revert uses the snapshot). | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/kernel/enabling-message-signaled-interrupts-in-the-registry>, <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/kernel/interrupt-affinity-and-priority>; never the boot-disk controller (spec section 6). |
| A6 | **`firewallRule`** only reduces exposure: iG Windows Tuner creates Block rules named `iGWindowsTuner-*` in its own group, or disables an existing rule group; it never creates Allow rules. **`scheduledTask`** only enables or disables existing tasks and refuses Defender, Windows Update, WaaSMedic, TPM, BitLocker, restore, time and AppID tasks. | No persistence and no security reduction (project rules). |
| A7 | **`exploitSystem` can only turn mitigations ON**; `processMitigation` OFF needs level Expert or Lab. Values are captured as ON/OFF/NOTSET; NOTSET is restored with `Set-ProcessMitigation -Remove -Disable <name>`. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/processmitigations/set-processmitigation> (example 4: `-Remove` restores the default). |
| A8 | **`appx` removal is `reversible: partial`**: revert re-registers the app from its install folder, else reinstalls it from the Store through winget (`storeId`); a removed provisioned copy is not restored for new profiles. Store, App Installer, Windows Security, shell, Xbox identity, Gaming Services and frameworks are protected. | Honest reversibility labels (schema v2). |
| A9 | **`winget`** runs only through `Invoke-IgwtWinget` with fixed arguments (`--exact`, `--silent`, `--accept-package-agreements`, `--accept-source-agreements`, `--disable-interactivity`); it refuses to run in TestMode, and on the development PC only `list`/`search` are allowed. | Spec section 3: network use only for user-initiated winget operations. |
| A10 | **`wufbPolicy`** limits: feature updates 0-365 days, quality updates 0-30 days, target release `Windows 11` + `NNH1/NNH2`. No "disable all"; pausing stays in Settings. Microsoft's pages list 0-30 or 0-35 for quality deferral; the spec's 30 is used. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/update/waas-configure-wufb> |
| A11 | **The Storage Sense tweaks now use the typed `storageSense` action.** They are new in 2.0, so no released snapshot depends on their old fingerprints; 1.0 tweaks keep their actions unchanged. | Readable catalog entries with range validation. |

## Hardware profile engine (2.0)

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | **Blocks are enforced in state detection**, not only in presets: a blocked item is Not applicable, so neither a preset nor `-Apply` can turn it on. An item that was applied before the overlay existed keeps its real state (On) with a "turning it off is recommended" reason, so it can still be reverted or reset. | A block is a hardware-safety rule (for example idle-disable on Raptor Lake); it must hold everywhere, but it must never trap a user with a setting they cannot undo. |
| H2 | **Your add-ons cannot bypass a block**; your removals and the preset's `exclude` always win over overlay adds. Overlay adds also respect the preset's level ceiling and anti-cheat policy, and never add Lab items. | Spec section 5 ("intent preset, hardware overlay, user add-ons") plus the preset safety rules from section 10. |
| H3 | **AMD X3D dual-CCD rule cites reviewer guidance.** AMD's chipset driver release notes document the 3D V-Cache Performance Optimizer, but no public AMD support page states the Balanced-plan / Game Bar requirement; reviewers (Notebookcheck) report it as AMD's recommendation, and forum results on other plans vary. The overlay is marked `basis: reviewer`. | Spec section 5 asks for the rule; the evidence is recorded honestly instead of overstated. |
| H4 | **SysMain rule is an iG Windows Tuner policy** (`basis: igwt`): no Microsoft page quantifies SysMain's benefit on hard disks or with little RAM, so the rule keeps the Windows default there. Memory compression has no catalog item to block yet. | Conservative default where documentation is missing. |
| H5 | **VM detection uses manufacturer/model strings, never `HypervisorPresent`**, which is also true on this PC because VBS runs Windows on the hypervisor. CPU-derived tags (`intel.hybrid`, `intel.raptorlake.desktop`) are not set inside a VM, where virtual processors look like cores without Hyper-Threading. | Avoids marking every VBS-enabled gaming PC as a VM. |
| H6 | **The VM overlay blocks adapter driver properties and power management (netAdapterAdvanced, netAdapterPower), USB/PCIe power and Wi-Fi**, but not per-interface TCP/IP settings (NetBIOS, delayed ACK). | Those registry settings exist on virtual adapters too; blocking them would hide valid security settings in Windows Sandbox runs. |
| H7 | **`intel.raptorlake.desktop` excludes mobile suffixes (H, HX, P, U)** even though HX parts share the Raptor Lake-S model number. | Intel's Vmin Shift statements concern 13th/14th gen desktop processors. The microcode health check is unchanged. |
| H8 | **Laptop rule blocks plan switches only.** iG Windows Tuner's power items write AC values exclusively, so DC battery saving is already never reduced; a matcher blocks any future item that writes DC values. The I226 overlay adds the EEE-off item, Intel's documented mitigation for random disconnects. | Spec section 5 laptop rules; the I226 source is an official Intel communication on Intel's community site. |
| H9 | **Hardware tags in item `hardware.tags`/`excludeTags` stay empty in the shipped catalog**; overlays carry the hardware logic. | Keeps each rule in one place with its source; item-level tags remain available for future hardware-specific items. |

## Cleaning engine (2.0)

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | **Allow-list rules plus a denylist in the deletion primitive.** Rules (`data\cleaner\*.json`) name the folders they may clean, and `Remove-IgwtCleanerFile` enforces the protections in code for every file: drive, Windows, Program Files, ProgramData, profile and user-document roots, Defender, OneDrive and Downloads. | A wrong or edited rule file must never be able to delete something important. The rule files are data; the guarantees live in the primitive and are covered by tests. |
| C2 | **Scan, then clean only the scanned set.** Each file is re-validated right before deletion: canonical path, root membership (roots re-resolved at clean time), denylist, parent reparse points, unchanged size and write time, minimum age. | Closes the time-of-check/time-of-use gap (for example a folder swapped for a junction after the scan) and keeps "what you saw is what gets deleted". |
| C3 | **No recursive deletes.** Only single files and empty folders are removed. | A recursive delete that meets a junction or a mis-resolved root is the classic cleaner disaster. |
| C4 | **`cleanmgr` is not used.** Its handlers are COM objects driven by `/sageset` registry state, are partly deprecated on Windows 11, and their deletions are not observable per file. | Every deletion must be logged and testable. |
| C5 | **Windows.old and upgrade leftovers are guidance only.** The rule shows the size and points to Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files. | Removing them needs ownership and ACL changes (the cleaner never takes ownership) and is Windows' own rollback mechanism. |
| C6 | **Component store and driver store use the supported tools.** `Repair-WindowsImage -StartComponentCleanup` (ResetBase only in the Expert rule), and `pnputil /delete-driver` **without `/force`** for packages that have a newer version and are not bound to a present device. | iG Windows Tuner never deletes inside WinSxS or the DriverStore directly; Windows refuses anything still in use. |
| C7 | **Browser rules clean caches only.** Cookies, history, passwords and session data are never deleted (a privacy wipe is deferred). Opera's profile lives in Roaming AppData, which is protected; only its Local AppData cache is cleaned. | Signing users out of everything is not "junk cleaning". |
| C8 | **Steam exceptions are in code**, not in rule files: `Steam\steamapps\shadercache`, `Steam\logs`, `Steam\dumps` and `Steam\appcache\httpcache` under Program Files are the only allowed paths inside Program Files. | Keeps Program Files protected even if a rule file is changed. |
| C9 | **Apps are never closed.** Rules list the processes that must not run (`requiresClosed`); while one runs, the rule reports "Close the app first" and is skipped. | Killing a game launcher or browser can lose user data. |
| C10 | **Below-normal thread priority, no I/O priority.** Setting the I/O priority would need a P/Invoke (`SetThreadInformation`), which conflicts with the "one P/Invoke" rule. | Same rule as E7. |
| C11 | **Spotify rule not shipped.** Its cache and offline-download folders overlap and differ by app version (desktop vs Store). | Users would lose downloaded songs; Spotify's own Settings > Storage > Clear cache is the safe path. |
| C12 | **The opt-in Downloads rule moves files to the Recycle Bin** and only touches files not created or changed for 60 days. | Downloads often holds files people meant to keep. |
| C13 | **The non-elevated GUI can clean user-level rules** (temp, caches) after a confirmation; admin rules show "Needs administrator". The CLI elevates only when a selected rule needs it. | Per-user caches belong to the signed-in user; elevating with a different admin account would clean the wrong profile. |
| C14 | **Storage Sense uses the documented Policy CSP values** under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\StorageSense` (absent by default). The Downloads threshold is an expert toggle outside every preset. While a policy is set, the Settings page shows "managed by your organization". | Policies are the only documented, revertible way to configure Storage Sense; per-user `StorageSense\Parameters` values are undocumented. |

## ASR Center and security modules (2.0)

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | **All 19 ASR rules live in `data\asr\rules.json`** with hint, description, gamer-impact note and level, Warn support, cloud dependency, server-only flag, recommended mode and sources. GUIDs, Warn limits (LSASS and Office injection do not support Warn), cloud dependencies and the Exchange-only webshell rule were checked against the Microsoft Learn reference (updated 9 Sep 2026). `Test-IgwtCatalog` validates the file and every `asrRule` action of the tweak catalog against it. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-reference> |
| R2 | **Modes: Not configured, Audit, Warn, Block. No explicit Off (code 0).** Not configured is the Windows default and Microsoft notes that Off can conflict with policies. Server-only rules and rules set by Group Policy or MDM are shown but never changed (local settings would be overwritten at startup). A previously captured Off is still restored exactly on revert. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-overview> (modes table); <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-configure> (policy precedence) |
| R3 | **Per-rule exclusions use the Group Policy registry settings**: `...\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\ASROnlyPerRuleExclusions` (value name = rule GUID, REG_SZ `path>path`) plus `ExploitGuard_ASR_ASROnlyPerRuleExclusions = 1`, as defined in this PC's `WindowsDefender.admx`. Microsoft documents per-rule exclusions only for Group Policy "and the corresponding registry settings", Intune and the Defender portal. The local `Add-MpPreference -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_RuleSpecificExclusions*` parameters exist but are undocumented, so they are only read (as administrator) to confirm Defender picked the values up. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-overview#file-and-folder-exclusions-for-asr-rules>; ADMX policy `ExploitGuard_ASR_ASROnlyPerRuleExclusions`. |
| R4 | **Exclusions are validated before anything changes.** Refused: drive roots, the Windows folder, the whole Program Files folders, folders or wildcards in user profiles and ProgramData, Downloads/Desktop/temp/browser-cache folders, user environment variables (Microsoft supports only system variables), relative segments, quotes and `>`. Folder exclusions must be two levels deep; a wildcard may stand for one folder below a named folder only. Antivirus exclusions (`ExclusionPath` and friends) are never added; a static test enforces it. | Microsoft: excluded files run without reports, and exclusions should be as narrow as possible. |
| R5 | **Every ASR Center change writes an `ASR` snapshot first**; revert goes through `Invoke-IgwtRevert` (Backups & Logs, `-RevertAll -Snapshot`). Rule GUIDs are re-validated against the catalog and registry paths come from code, never from the file. A revert writes its own snapshot so it can be undone. | Same reversibility rule as every tweak. |
| R6 | **Recommendations for a gaming PC:** the three standard protection rules and rules without gamer impact (email, scripts, obfuscation, USB) in Block, which matches the 1.0 `sec.asr-baseline`; rules that can catch games, launchers or mods (prevalence/age, ransomware heuristics, copied system tools, PsExec/WMI) and the Office/Adobe rules in Audit; Safe Mode reboot in Audit because Microsoft lists it among the rules to test first. "Apply recommendations" never lowers a rule. Validation refuses Block as the recommendation for medium or high gamer impact. | Microsoft's guidance: standard rules straight to Block, other rules audited first. |
| R7 | **Audit view recommendations:** promote a quiet Audit rule only after at least 7 days of Defender log coverage (Warn first for medium/high gamer impact); suggest a per-rule exclusion only for the exact file, only when it passes R4, never for Windows paths; LSASS events are expected noise (Microsoft). Command lines from events are not shown. Since platform 4.18.26060 a Warn bypass needs administrator approval, which the texts mention. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-windows-events> |
| R8 | **Security items added:** exploit protection defaults (repair-only: "use default" counts as on through `equivalentOn: ["NOTSET"]`, so nothing is written on a healthy PC; Mandatory ASLR stays at its default), WDigest off (repair-only), no anonymous enumeration, NTLMv2 only (level 5, DISA STIG; Microsoft's minimum countermeasure is level 3), Windows Script Host off (Tier B: Microsoft's documentation is archived, CISA warns some tools use WSH), outbound firewall blocks for mshta/wscript/cscript/regsvr32/certutil (Tier B, MITRE ATT&CK), Print Spooler without inbound clients (Standard) and Print Spooler off (Advanced, only for PCs that never print). | Each item raises security, is anti-cheat safe and fully reversible. |
| R9 | **Not added:** SSDP/UPnP and Teredo off (Xbox networking, party chat and some games' NAT traversal depend on them); WinRM and Remote Registry off (no listener by default / already disabled on Windows 11, so no benefit); mDNS off (undocumented value); USB storage deny and removable-media execute deny (the USB ASR rule covers untrusted programs without breaking USB drives); Office macro policies (per Office version, read-only guidance later); WDAC policies (Lab, deferred); per-app exploit protection templates (deferred: games and anti-cheat react badly to forced mitigations). | Scope rule: only clearly safe and beneficial items, nothing that breaks games or anti-cheat. |
| R10 | **Security score is a read-only weighted checklist** (25 checks, every one with a hint, description and fix route). Pass = weight, Warn = half, Fail = 0; not applicable, Group Policy/MDM-managed and unreadable checks are left out. Smart App Control and Credential Guard are shown but not scored: SAC cannot be turned back on without a reset, and Credential Guard is not part of Windows 11 Pro. | A score must not punish what the user cannot change. |
| R11 | **Network surface lists TCP listeners and UDP endpoints below the dynamic port range (49152+)**, with owning program, services and scope. Listening is not the same as reachable; the firewall decides. Well-known ports and the Print Spooler's dynamic RPC endpoint point to the catalog item that reduces them. | Ephemeral UDP client sockets are noise. |
| R12 | **The cleaner's `Test-IgwtPathUnder` is shared**; a static test now fails when any function name is defined twice, because a later file would silently replace the earlier definition. Another static test refuses `$name?` inside strings (PowerShell reads it as a variable named `name?`). | Both bugs happened during phase 5 and were caught by the suite. |

## Expert controls and inspectors (2.0)

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| X1 | **Inspectors first, edits second.** Six read-only inspectors (power plan, interrupts, network queues, kernel and memory, timer, crash and page file) show current values next to Windows defaults. The only direct editor is the processor power settings editor; every other change goes through a catalog item with its own snapshot and revert. | Spec section 6; keeps every write in the audited catalog model. |
| X2 | **Power plan editor scope:** the 16 processor settings in `data\power\processor.json` (EPP, boost mode and policy, min/max state, core parking min cores and concurrency, idle promote/demote, hybrid scheduling policies), level Expert, `-AcknowledgeRisk` or a GUI confirmation, snapshot operation `Power`, revert through `Invoke-IgwtRevert`. Ranges come from what `powercfg /qh` reports on this PC; hardware overlays block settings (core parking and hybrid scheduling on Intel hybrid CPUs, core parking on AMD dual-CCD X3D, battery values on laptops). Processor idle disable is never editable. | Microsoft Learn PPM option pages; overlays H1/H2. |
| X3 | **Defaults:** Windows' stored defaults (`DefaultPowerSchemeValues`) for built-in plans; a plan copy is compared with the built-in plan that has the same name resource. Windows stores no defaults for Ultimate Performance and its hidden base plan reports UNKNOWN, so Balanced is shown as a labelled reference there. | Verified on this PC: the Ultimate copy and its base have no stored defaults. |
| X4 | **powercfg output is parsed without labels:** indentation, GUIDs, upper-case aliases and hex values only, so localized Windows works; UNKNOWN indexes are treated as unknown. | Labels are localized; a test uses German-style labels. |
| X5 | **Interrupt edits:** only `gfx.gpu-msi` (Expert, Tier B, reboot, MSISupported = 1 where the driver declares MSI support) is catalogued. On this PC the GPU, NIC and USB controller already use MSI, which is typical of current hardware. Affinity policy presets are not catalogued (Microsoft recommends the default policy) and manual core pinning (AssignmentSetOverride) is rejected. The inspector reads the mode in use from the allocated interrupt resources (message-signaled IRQs are reported at 0x80000000 and above). | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/kernel/interrupt-affinity-and-priority> |
| X6 | **NIC queues are inspector-only:** RSS placement, queues and buffers with the driver's range and the adapter's discarded-packet counter. Advice to raise receive buffers appears only when packets are actually discarded; the "keep RSS off core 0" advice points to the driver's own setting when it exists (the Marvell AQtion on this PC does not expose it). | Driver-specific keywords and ranges; evidence before edits. |
| X7 | **The current timer resolution is not displayed.** Reading it needs the undocumented `NtQueryTimerResolution`, which would add a second P/Invoke (same rule as E4/E7). The timer inspector explains the per-process behaviour and points to `powercfg /energy`. | One documented P/Invoke. |
| X8 | **Kernel and memory inspector is read-only:** values are annotated from `data\inspectors\kernel.json` with meaning, default and either the catalog item (the only way to change them) or the rejected entry that explains them. Undocumented values are listed so users can see what other tools changed. | Spec section 6 ("editable only if catalogued"). |
| X9 | **New System category:** page file managed by Windows (Standard; never disabled, a fixed size is not offered because Microsoft recommends system-managed), small memory dumps (Advanced), verbose status messages (Advanced) and stop-code parameters on the blue screen (Advanced, Tier B: `DisplayParameters` is not documented by Microsoft; source WinUtil with attribution). | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/performance/introduction-to-the-page-file>, <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/performance/memory-dump-file-options> |
| X10 | **Lab items from spec section 6 are rejected, not implemented:** hypervisor launch type off (a BCD write, A1, and it breaks VBS, FACEIT and Vanguard On-Demand), processor idle disable (heat and Raptor Lake voltage risk for no measurable game benefit) and manual interrupt affinity pinning. All are documented in `data\rejected.json` with the other section 6 rejections (test signing and friends, IFEO, registry cleaners, hosts-file blocking, Prefetch cleaning, manual WinSxS/Installer deletion, disabling IPv6). | Scope rule: only clearly safe and beneficial items. |
| X11 | **`power.show-processor-settings` is Advanced, not Expert:** it only clears the hidden attribute so the settings appear in Power Options; values do not change. | Visibility carries no risk. |

## Management and diagnostic modules (2.0)

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | **One audited change path.** Services, tasks, inbox apps, optional features, capabilities and app firewall rules change only through `Invoke-IgwtManagedChange`, which turns the request into a synthetic action of an existing, tested type (service, scheduledTask, appx, optionalFeature, capability) or a firewall rule enable flag, writes a snapshot (operation `Manage`) first and reverts through `Invoke-IgwtRevert`. On revert the action is rebuilt from the stored kind, target and value and validated again, so an edited snapshot cannot reach a protected target. | Same snapshot and revert model as every other write; tested handlers instead of new ones. |
| M2 | **Protected services** (`data\manage\services.json`, checked by `Test-IgwtManageCatalog`): the core list from spec section 12 (RPC/DCOM/LSM/SAM/Power/PlugPlay/ProfSvc/Schedule, BFE/MpsSvc/WinDefend and security services, EventLog/Winmgmt/CryptSvc, audio, Dhcp/Dnscache/nsi, TrustedInstaller), plus Windows Update, app deployment, GPU driver services and the anti-cheat services. Drivers are never changed; Manual is suggested over Disabled. | Spec section 12. |
| M3 | **Tasks are disabled or enabled, never created or deleted.** Security, update, recovery, TPM/BitLocker and anti-cheat tasks are refused (the existing `scheduledTask` protection list plus an anti-cheat name pattern). The curated telemetry set is catalog item `privacy.telemetry-tasks-off` (Advanced, Tier B, measure): Compatibility Appraiser (and its Exp variant), CEIP Consolidator and UsbCeip, Autochk Proxy, disk diagnostic data collector and the two Feedback SIUF tasks; missing tasks are skipped. | Microsoft documents these as telemetry and CEIP components; the performance effect is situational. |
| M4 | **Persistence Inspector is read-only** (Run/RunOnce incl. WOW6432Node, Startup folders, non-Microsoft services and drivers, non-Microsoft tasks, WMI event consumers, Winlogon Shell/Userinit, IFEO Debugger, AppInit_DLLs, browser extensions) with Authenticode status. "Microsoft" means a valid Microsoft signature and a Microsoft company name in the file, so WHQL-signed third-party drivers are listed. Actions are limited to the documented disable mechanisms that already exist: StartupApproved for startup entries, service startup type and task disable, each with a snapshot. WMI subscriptions, IFEO and AppInit entries are reported, never edited. | Spec section 12; deleting persistence is antivirus work. |
| M5 | **Apps:** inbox Appx removal per user and optionally provisioned, with the reversibility note (re-register or reinstall from the Store). Store, App Installer, Xbox Identity Provider, Gaming Services, Windows Security, WebView2, frameworks and system (shell) packages are refused. Win32 apps are listed only; their own uninstaller removes them. | Spec section 12; Win32 uninstallers are not reversible by iG Windows Tuner. |
| M6 | **Features and capabilities manager** refuses Defender, .NET 4, WSL and the virtualization platform, Print to PDF, search, languages, Notepad, shell components and the OpenSSH client. Reading them needs administrator rights. | Removing these breaks security, games or the shell. |
| M7 | **Windows Update: read-only status plus one catalog item.** Status shows services, pending restart, Windows Update for Business policy values and history from the Windows Update Agent (query only). "Last successful update" ignores Defender definition updates. The only new policy item is `privacy.defer-feature-90` (feature updates 90 days, Tier A); quality (security) updates are never deferred and Windows Update is never disabled. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/update/waas-configure-wufb> |
| M8 | **Network toolkit:** the adapter inspector shows every advanced property with a description (standardized NDIS keywords from `data\manage\nic-keywords.json`, vendor keywords marked as such) and changes nothing. The DNS benchmark and the latency/jitter/loss test run only when the user starts them. Firewall rules shipped with Windows (resource-string groups) and iG Windows Tuner's own rules are shown but never changed; app rules can be enabled or disabled; nothing is deleted. The hosts file is read-only and entries other than localhost are flagged (blocks of Microsoft endpoints separately, see `rejected.hosts-telemetry-block`). | Spec section 12. |
| M9 | **DPC and ISR from raw counters.** Formatted WMI counters need two reads in one query and returned 0 here, so percentages are computed from raw `Win32_PerfRawData_PerfOS_Processor` deltas (100 ns timers against `Timestamp_Sys100NS`) and top processes from CPU-time deltas over the same window. Windows only exposes totals; LatencyMon or WPA name the driver. | Verified on this PC against `Get-Counter`. |
| M10 | **Crashes:** BugCheck (WER-SystemErrorReporting 1001), Kernel-Power 41, EventLog 6008 and application crashes (1000), plus the minidump list; minidumps are never deleted here. **Boot performance** reads Diagnostics-Performance event 100 (administrator rights). **Drivers:** Intel chipset INFs use the placeholder date 1968-07-18 on purpose and are not flagged as old. | Event IDs from Microsoft documentation; Intel INF convention. |
| M11 | **System report** combines the health report, diagnostics, Windows Update, services and persistence summaries, drivers and the active items into one self-contained HTML (no scripts) or JSON file; each failing section is recorded instead of stopping the report. It contains the computer name and installed software, which the report says. | Spec section 12. |

## Rename to iG Windows Tuner (2026-10-20)

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | **Names:** product and GUI "iG Windows Tuner"; files and module `iGWindowsTuner`; command and variable prefix `Igwt`; environment variables `IGWT_`; schema value `igwt`; data root `%ProgramData%\iGWindowsTuner`; created objects `iGWindowsTuner-...`. | One name everywhere; `Igwt` keeps command names readable. |
| N2 | **Old data keeps working, read-only:** the old data root `%ProgramData%\AegisTune` is a legacy source for backups and the pending-restart state, never a write target; snapshots with `tool: "AegisTune"` are accepted; QoS policies named `AegisTune-<game>` count as applied and are changed or removed under that name. Files are not moved, so their protected ACL (the trust check for restores) stays intact. | On the development PC 27 backups and four `AegisTune-*` QoS policies existed before the rename. |
| N3 | **Owned firewall rules** are now named `iGWindowsTuner-...`. No `AegisTune-*` rules existed, so old firewall snapshot entries (none on the development PC) would not match the renamed catalog actions. | Action fingerprints include the rule name. |
| N4 | **Historical files keep the old name:** the frozen 1.0 fixtures in `tests\fixtures\v1` and the archive `AegisTune-v1-baseline.zip`. | They document what 1.0 shipped. |

|---|---|
| `net.wifi-disable` | The Intel AX211 is "Not Present" (disabled in firmware), so there is no Wi-Fi adapter to disable. |
```

`docs/HARDWARE.md`:

```md
# iG Windows Tuner hardware profile and overlays

> Generated by `tools\Build-Docs.ps1` from `data\hardware\*.json`. Do not edit by hand.

iG Windows Tuner detects hardware tags read-only (`.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Hardware`) and applies hardware overlays. Presets are resolved in this order: **intent preset, then hardware overlays, then your own add-ons and removals**. An overlay can block items (they become Not applicable on that hardware; an item that is already applied can still be turned off), add items to presets (only when the preset's level ceiling and anti-cheat policy allow it, and never when the preset excludes them) and show guidance in the report and in preset dry runs.

## Hardware tags

| Tag | Name | Detected when | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `intel.hybrid` | Intel hybrid CPU (P-cores and E-cores) | Intel CPU with fewer threads than twice its cores: P-cores have Hyper-Threading, E-cores do not (12th gen and newer). | 12th to 14th gen Core and Core Ultra. Thread Director and the Windows scheduler stay in charge of core placement. |
| `intel.raptorlake.desktop` | Intel Raptor Lake desktop CPU | Family 6, model 183 or 191 (Raptor Lake-S), 13th/14th gen name without a mobile suffix, not inside a virtual machine. | 13th and 14th gen desktop Core. The microcode 0x12F (Vmin Shift) check runs, and idle-voltage-raising items are blocked. |
| `amd.zen` | AMD Ryzen (Zen) | AMD Ryzen processor. | AMD Ryzen desktop or laptop CPU. The AMD chipset driver is checked and the power plan follows the preset. |
| `amd.x3d.singleccd` | AMD Ryzen X3D (single CCD) | Ryzen 5/7 X3D models with a single core complex. | Single-CCD X3D CPU such as the 7800X3D or 9800X3D. Chipset driver check plus normal plan selection. |
| `amd.x3d.dualccd` | AMD Ryzen X3D (dual CCD) | Ryzen 9 X3D models with two core complexes, only one of which carries 3D V-Cache. | 7900X3D, 7950X3D, 9900X3D, 9950X3D. Keeps Balanced with core parking and Game Bar game detection for the V-Cache CCD. |
| `gpu.nvidia` | NVIDIA GPU | Active GPU with PCI vendor ID 10DE (NVIDIA). | An NVIDIA GeForce or RTX GPU is active. Guidance covers Reflex and driver settings; driver profiles are never written. |
| `gpu.amd` | AMD Radeon GPU | Active GPU with PCI vendor ID 1002 (AMD). | An AMD Radeon GPU is active. Guidance covers Anti-Lag and driver settings; driver profiles are never written. |
| `gpu.intel` | Intel GPU | Active GPU with PCI vendor ID 8086 (Intel). | An Intel integrated or Arc GPU is active. Guidance only; driver settings are never written. |
| `gpu.intel.arc` | Intel Arc discrete GPU | Intel Arc A- or B-series discrete GPU (for example A770 or B580); integrated 'Arc Graphics' does not match. | Intel Arc graphics card. Resizable BAR is required for good performance, so its status is checked and shown. |
| `formfactor.desktop` | Desktop PC | No battery, no portable chassis type, not a virtual machine. | No battery detected. Desktop power plans and AC-only tuning apply. |
| `formfactor.laptop` | Laptop | A system battery or a portable chassis type, and not a virtual machine. | A battery is present. AC and DC values are separate, and battery-saving behaviour on DC is never reduced. |
| `power.modernstandby` | Modern Standby (S0) | 'powercfg /a' lists Standby (S0 Low Power Idle) as available. | The PC uses Modern Standby. Windows power-mode overlays are preferred over custom power plans. |
| `nic.intel.i225` | Intel I225 Ethernet | Intel Ethernet Controller I225 (name or PCI device ID). | Intel I225 2.5 GbE controller. Known-issue notes and the vendor's advanced-property keywords apply. |
| `nic.intel.i226` | Intel I226 Ethernet | Intel Ethernet Controller I226 (name or PCI device ID). | Intel I226 2.5 GbE controller. Known-issue notes and the vendor's advanced-property keywords apply. |
| `nic.realtek` | Realtek Ethernet | Network controller with PCI vendor ID 10EC (Realtek). | Realtek Ethernet controller. Vendor-specific advanced-property names and known issues apply. |
| `nic.marvell` | Marvell / Aquantia Ethernet | Network controller with PCI vendor ID 1D6A (Aquantia, now Marvell) or 11AB (Marvell). | Marvell (Aquantia) multi-gigabit Ethernet controller. Vendor keyword mapping and known issues apply. |
| `nic.killer` | Killer networking | Network controller named Killer. | Killer Ethernet or Wi-Fi with its traffic-prioritisation software. Conflicting QoS items are flagged. |
| `storage.nvme` | NVMe system disk | The disk holding the Windows partition reports bus type NVMe. | Windows runs from an NVMe SSD. Storage items keep TRIM and the default write caching. |
| `storage.sata` | SATA SSD system disk | The Windows disk is a SATA solid-state drive. | Windows runs from a SATA SSD. Storage items keep TRIM and the default write caching. |
| `storage.hdd` | Hard disk system drive | The Windows disk reports media type HDD. | Windows runs from a spinning hard disk. SysMain and memory compression stay on because they help here. |
| `ram.lt16` | Less than 16 GB of RAM | Installed memory below 16 GB. | Under 16 GB of memory. SysMain and memory compression stay on, and memory-hungry items are blocked. |
| `ram.16` | 16 GB of RAM | Installed memory from 16 GB up to (not including) 32 GB. | 16 GB of installed memory. Standard memory behaviour applies. |
| `ram.32` | 32 GB of RAM | Installed memory from 32 GB up to (not including) 64 GB. | 32 GB of installed memory. Standard memory behaviour applies. |
| `ram.64plus` | 64 GB or more of RAM | Installed memory of 64 GB or more. | 64 GB or more of installed memory. Standard memory behaviour applies. |
| `vm` | Virtual machine | System manufacturer or model names a hypervisor (Hyper-V 'Virtual Machine', VMware, VirtualBox, KVM, QEMU, Xen, Parallels). HypervisorPresent is not used: it is also true on PCs with VBS. | Running inside a virtual machine. Hardware-level items (devices, firmware, power hardware) are disabled. |

## Overlays

### Intel hybrid CPU: scheduler stays in charge

`overlay.intel-hybrid` | tags: `intel.hybrid` | basis: vendor

*Keeps Power Throttling on and blocks core-parking and heterogeneous-scheduling overrides on P-core/E-core CPUs.*

Intel Thread Director feeds the Windows scheduler, which places foreground work on P-cores and background work on E-cores. Intel's guidance is to avoid hard affinities and let the OS schedule; Power Throttling is part of that placement. So presets keep Power Throttling on, and items that change core parking or the heterogeneous scheduling policy are blocked on this hardware.

- Blocks any item with an action where type = powercfgSetting; setting = 7f2f5cfa-f10c-4823-b5e1-e93ae85f46b5 / 93b8b6dc-0698-4d1c-9ee4-0644e900c85d / bae08b81-2d5e-4688-ad6a-13243356654b / 0cc5b647-c1df-4637-891a-dec35c318583 / 0cc5b647-c1df-4637-891a-dec35c318584 / ea062031-0e34-4ff1-9b6d-eb1059334028 / ea062031-0e34-4ff1-9b6d-eb1059334029
- Adds to presets: `power.power-throttling-on`
- Guidance: Do not pin games to P-cores with affinity tools; Windows 11 and Thread Director already prefer P-cores for foreground work.

**Sources:** <https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/guide/12th-gen-intel-core-processor-gamedev-guide.html> <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/quality-of-service>

### Raptor Lake desktop: Vmin Shift protection

`overlay.raptorlake-voltage` | tags: `intel.raptorlake.desktop` | basis: vendor

*Checks for microcode 0x12F or newer and blocks items that keep cores out of idle states on 13th/14th gen desktop CPUs.*

Intel traced Vmin Shift Instability on 13th and 14th gen desktop processors to elevated core voltage over time and fixed it with microcode updates up to 0x12F. Keeping cores out of idle states (processor idle disable) holds them at active voltage, so such items are blocked here. The health report checks the microcode revision; Intel recommends the latest BIOS with the Intel Default Settings profile.

- Blocks any item with an action where type = powercfgSetting; setting = 5d76a2ca-e8c0-402f-a133-2158492d58ad
- Guidance: Keep the motherboard BIOS current (microcode 0x12F or newer) and use the Intel Default Settings profile. iG Windows Tuner never changes firmware, voltages or power limits.

**Sources:** <https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000102331/processors.html>

### AMD X3D dual-CCD: keep V-Cache core steering working

`overlay.amd-x3d-dualccd` | tags: `amd.x3d.dualccd` | basis: reviewer

*Blocks High/Ultimate Performance plans and core-parking changes so the AMD driver can steer games to the V-Cache CCD.*

On dual-CCD X3D processors the AMD 3D V-Cache Performance Optimizer (part of the AMD chipset driver) parks the second CCD while a game runs, which needs the Balanced plan with core parking active and Windows game detection. High and Ultimate Performance plans disable core parking, so they and core-parking changes are blocked; Game Mode is added to presets.

- Blocks: `power.high-performance-plan`, `power.ultimate-plan`
- Blocks any item with an action where type = powercfgSetting; setting = 0cc5b647-c1df-4637-891a-dec35c318583 / 0cc5b647-c1df-4637-891a-dec35c318584 / ea062031-0e34-4ff1-9b6d-eb1059334028 / ea062031-0e34-4ff1-9b6d-eb1059334029
- Blocks any item with an action where type = appx; name = Microsoft.XboxGamingOverlay
- Adds to presets: `gfx.game-mode`
- Guidance: Install the current AMD chipset driver (it contains the 3D V-Cache Performance Optimizer), keep Game Mode on and keep the Xbox Game Bar app installed and updated.

**Sources:** <https://www.amd.com/en/resources/support-articles/release-notes/RN-RYZEN-CHIPSET-7-11-26-2142.html> <https://www.notebookcheck.net/AMD-Ryzen-9-9950X3D-Review-Ryzen-7-9800X3D-levels-of-gaming-performance-and-power-efficiency-for-50-markup-over-the-Ryzen-9-9950X.976049.0.html>

### AMD Ryzen: chipset driver

`overlay.amd-chipset` | tags: `amd.zen` | basis: vendor

*Reminds you to install the AMD chipset driver, which provides Ryzen power management and scheduler support.*

The AMD chipset driver package installs the Ryzen power-management and scheduling components (including the 3D V-Cache Performance Optimizer on dual-CCD X3D models). Windows Update's generic drivers do not include all of them, so the report points to AMD's package. The power plan follows the selected preset.

- Guidance: Install the latest AMD chipset driver from amd.com or your motherboard vendor.

**Sources:** <https://www.amd.com/en/resources/support-articles/release-notes/RN-RYZEN-CHIPSET-7-11-26-2142.html>

### Modern Standby: Balanced plan and power mode

`overlay.modern-standby` | tags: `power.modernstandby` | basis: vendor

*Modern Standby PCs only support Balanced-derived plans, so plan switches are blocked; use the Windows power mode instead.*

Microsoft documents that devices with Modern Standby only allow the Balanced power plan or plans derived from it, and that performance is tuned with the power mode slider (overlays on top of Balanced). Switching to High or Ultimate Performance is therefore blocked; choose Best performance under Settings > System > Power & battery > Power mode.

- Blocks: `power.high-performance-plan`, `power.ultimate-plan`
- Guidance: Use Settings > System > Power & battery > Power mode (Best performance while gaming on AC).

**Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/customize-power-slider>

### Laptop: never reduce battery saving

`overlay.laptop-battery` | tags: `formfactor.laptop` | basis: vendor

*Blocks power-plan switches on laptops; iG Windows Tuner power items only change AC values, so battery (DC) behaviour stays.*

Switching the whole power plan also changes battery (DC) behaviour, so High and Ultimate Performance plans are blocked on laptops; Microsoft's model for portables is the Balanced plan plus the power mode slider. iG Windows Tuner's power settings write AC values only, so DC battery saving is never reduced, and any future item that writes DC values is blocked too.

- Blocks: `power.high-performance-plan`, `power.ultimate-plan`
- Blocks any item with an action where type = powercfgSetting; fieldPresent = dc
- Guidance: Plug in for gaming sessions and use the power mode slider; keep the battery saver behaviour on DC.

**Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/customize-power-slider>

### Slow disk or little RAM: keep SysMain

`overlay.keep-sysmain` | tags: `storage.hdd`, `ram.lt16` | basis: igwt

*Keeps SysMain (prefetching) on when Windows runs from a hard disk or the PC has less than 16 GB of RAM.*

SysMain preloads frequently used programs into free memory. Its benefit is largest when the system disk is slow and smallest on NVMe with plenty of RAM, which is the only case where iG Windows Tuner offers turning it off. On a hard disk or below 16 GB of memory the Windows default is kept, so the SysMain item is blocked.

- Blocks: `privacy.sysmain-off`
- Blocks any item with an action where type = service; name = SysMain
- Guidance: SysMain and memory compression stay at their Windows defaults on this hardware.

**Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/security/windows-services/security-guidelines-for-disabling-system-services-in-windows-server>

### Virtual machine: no hardware-level items

`overlay.virtual-machine` | tags: `vm` | basis: igwt

*Inside a virtual machine, items that change physical network adapters, USB, PCIe or Wi-Fi hardware are not applicable.*

A virtual machine exposes virtual devices: synthetic network adapters without vendor driver properties, no physical PCIe links or USB controllers to power-manage, and no Wi-Fi radio. Items that change such hardware (adapter driver properties and power management, USB and PCIe power, Wi-Fi, device interrupts) are blocked. Per-interface TCP/IP settings such as NetBIOS stay available because they exist on virtual adapters too.

- Blocks: `net.wifi-disable`, `power.usb-selective-suspend-off`, `power.pcie-aspm-off`
- Blocks any item with an action where type = netAdapterAdvanced / netAdapterPower / deviceInterrupt / bcd
- Blocks any item with an action where type = custom; handler = WifiAdapter

**Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/virtualization/hyper-v-on-windows/about/>

### Intel Arc: Resizable BAR

`overlay.intel-arc` | tags: `gpu.intel.arc` | basis: vendor

*Intel Arc cards need Resizable BAR for their intended performance. Enable it in the BIOS if the report shows it off.*

Intel states that Resizable BAR must be enabled for optimal performance with Arc graphics; without it the card works but can be much slower. iG Windows Tuner does not change firmware settings, so this overlay adds guidance to the report and preset previews.

- Guidance: Enable Resizable BAR (and Above 4G Decoding) in the motherboard BIOS for Intel Arc graphics.

**Sources:** <https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000092416.html>

### NVIDIA GPU: Reflex

`overlay.nvidia-reflex` | tags: `gpu.nvidia` | basis: vendor

*Turn on NVIDIA Reflex in supported games; it lowers latency more than OS tweaks. Driver profiles are never written.*

NVIDIA Reflex reduces render latency inside supported games and usually matters more than any Windows setting. iG Windows Tuner only shows this guidance and the read-only NVIDIA checklist; it never writes driver profiles.

- Guidance: Enable NVIDIA Reflex in games that support it (Dota 2, CS2, VALORANT and others).

**Sources:** <https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/technologies/reflex/>

### AMD Radeon GPU: Anti-Lag 2

`overlay.amd-anti-lag` | tags: `gpu.amd` | basis: vendor

*Turn on AMD Anti-Lag 2 in supported games to lower input latency. Driver settings are never written.*

AMD Anti-Lag 2 is an in-game latency reduction for Radeon GPUs in supported titles. iG Windows Tuner only shows this guidance; it never writes AMD driver settings.

- Guidance: Enable AMD Anti-Lag 2 in games that support it (for example Counter-Strike 2 and Dota 2).

**Sources:** <https://www.amd.com/en/products/software/adrenalin/radeon-software-anti-lag.html>

### Intel I225 Ethernet: firmware and driver

`overlay.intel-i225` | tags: `nic.intel.i225` | basis: vendor

*Intel I225 connection drops are fixed by updating the controller NVM firmware and the LAN driver from your board vendor.*

Intel's support article for the I225-V covers connection drops while gaming and links that are not detected. The fix is to update the controller's NVM with the OEM's firmware tool first, then install the latest LAN driver after a clean uninstall. iG Windows Tuner shows this as guidance; it does not flash firmware.

- Guidance: Update the I225 NVM firmware with your motherboard vendor's tool, then install the latest Intel LAN driver.

**Sources:** <https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000057261/ethernet-products/gigabit-ethernet-controllers-up-to-2-5gbe.html>

### Intel I226 Ethernet: Energy Efficient Ethernet off

`overlay.intel-i226` | tags: `nic.intel.i226` | basis: vendor

*Intel's mitigation for I226-V random connection drops is turning Energy Efficient Ethernet off; presets include it here.*

Intel acknowledged random connection drops on I226-V controllers and named disabling Energy Efficient Ethernet (EEE) as the mitigation. The EEE-off item is therefore added to presets on this hardware, together with guidance to install the current driver from the board vendor.

- Adds to presets: `net.eee-off`
- Guidance: Install the latest I226 driver from your motherboard vendor or Intel.

**Sources:** <https://community.intel.com/t5/Ethernet-Products/Intel-Communication-Intel-Ethernet-Controller-I226-Series-Random/td-p/1453177>

### Killer networking: one traffic prioritiser

`overlay.killer` | tags: `nic.killer` | basis: vendor

*Killer's Prioritization Engine already ranks game traffic; use it or Windows game QoS, not both, to avoid conflicts.*

The Intel Killer Control Center assigns a priority to each packet and throttles lower-priority apps when bandwidth is nearly full. iG Windows Tuner's game QoS item marks game packets with DSCP through Windows policies; running both can give confusing results, so pick one. This overlay only adds guidance.

- Guidance: Use either the Killer Prioritization Engine or iG Windows Tuner's game QoS item (net.qos-dscp-games), not both.

**Sources:** <https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000058936/wireless/wireless-software.html>

### Realtek and Marvell Ethernet: vendor driver

`overlay.vendor-nic-driver` | tags: `nic.realtek`, `nic.marvell` | basis: vendor

*Install the vendor's own LAN driver so the standard advanced properties (EEE, RSS, interrupt moderation) are exposed.*

iG Windows Tuner changes network adapter settings through the standardized advanced-property keywords such as *EEE, *RSS and *InterruptModeration. Vendor drivers from Realtek and Marvell expose these; generic or very old drivers may not, in which case the items show as not applicable. Use the driver from the board or adapter vendor.

- Guidance: Install the current LAN driver from your motherboard or adapter vendor (Realtek or Marvell).

**Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/network/standardized-inf-keywords-for-power-management>

## Basis

- **vendor**: documented by the hardware or OS vendor.
- **reviewer**: the vendor's guidance as published in reviewer guides and reviews (no public vendor support page found; see `docs\DECISIONS.md`).
- **igwt**: a conservative iG Windows Tuner rule that keeps the Windows default on this hardware.
```
