`docs/INSPECTORS.md`:

```md
# Expert inspectors and the power plan editor

> Generated by `tools\Build-Docs.ps1` from `data\power\processor.json` and `data\inspectors\kernel.json`. Do not edit by hand.

Read-only inspectors (GUI page *Expert Inspectors*, `-Inspect All|Power|Interrupts|Network|Kernel|Timer|Crash`) show the settings engineers tune next to the Windows default. Only the processor power settings below can be edited here, with a snapshot first (`-PowerSetting <alias> -Ac <n> [-Dc <n>] -AcknowledgeRisk`, `-DryRun` to validate); everything else changes only through catalog items.

## Power plan editor

- Values are checked against the range `powercfg /qh` reports for the active plan.
- Hardware overlays apply: on Intel hybrid CPUs core parking and hybrid scheduling settings are blocked; on AMD dual-CCD X3D CPUs core parking is blocked; on laptops battery (DC) values are blocked.
- Processor idle disable is never editable (see `rejected.processor-idle-disable`).
- Defaults come from Windows' stored plan defaults; a plan copy is compared with the built-in plan it came from; Ultimate Performance has no stored defaults, so Balanced is shown as a labelled reference.

| Alias | Group | Level | Hint | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PERFEPP` | Performance state | Expert | Energy performance preference (0-100 %). Lower favours performance, higher saves power. Only CPUs with CPPC v2 use it. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-perf-state-engine-perfenergypreference> |
| `PERFEPP1` | Performance state | Expert | Energy performance preference for efficiency-class (E) cores (0-100 %). Lower favours performance. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-perf-state-engine-perfenergypreference> |
| `PERFBOOSTMODE` | Boost | Expert | How the CPU boosts above base clock: Disabled, Enabled, Aggressive and efficient variants. Disabled caps the CPU at base clock. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-perf-state-engine-perfboostmode> |
| `PERFBOOSTPOL` | Boost | Expert | How strongly the OS uses boost (0-100 %) on processors where Windows controls boost directly. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/configure-processor-power-management-options> |
| `PROCTHROTTLEMIN` | Performance state | Expert | Minimum processor state (%). 100 keeps clocks high at idle: more heat and power, rarely a measurable gain. Measure. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-perf-state-engine-minperformance> |
| `PROCTHROTTLEMIN1` | Performance state | Expert | Minimum processor state for efficiency-class (E) cores (%). | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-perf-state-engine-minperformance> |
| `PROCTHROTTLEMAX` | Performance state | Expert | Maximum processor state (%). Below 100 caps clocks and usually disables boost. Useful to limit heat, not for speed. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-perf-state-engine-maxperformance> |
| `PROCTHROTTLEMAX1` | Performance state | Expert | Maximum processor state for efficiency-class (E) cores (%). | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-perf-state-engine-maxperformance> |
| `CPMINCORES` | Core parking | Expert | Minimum share of cores kept unparked (%). Blocked on Intel hybrid and AMD dual-CCD X3D CPUs, where parking drives placement. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-core-parking-cpmincores> |
| `CPMINCORES1` | Core parking | Expert | Minimum share of efficiency-class (E) cores kept unparked (%). Blocked on hybrid and dual-CCD X3D CPUs. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-core-parking-cpmincores> |
| `CPCONCURRENCY` | Core parking | Expert | Core parking concurrency threshold (%): how busy the unparked cores must be before more cores are unparked. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-core-parking-cpconcurrency> |
| `IDLEPROMOTE` | Idle | Expert | Idle promote threshold (%): how idle a core must be before Windows moves it to a deeper idle state. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-perf-state-engine-idlepromotethreshold> |
| `IDLEDEMOTE` | Idle | Expert | Idle demote threshold (%): how busy a core must be before Windows moves it to a shallower idle state. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/options-for-perf-state-engine-idledemotethreshold> |
| `HETEROPOLICY` | Hybrid scheduling | Expert | Heterogeneous policy in effect on P-core/E-core CPUs. Blocked on Intel hybrid CPUs: Windows and Thread Director decide. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/configure-processor-power-management-options> |
| `SCHEDPOLICY` | Hybrid scheduling | Expert | Where long-running threads may run on hybrid CPUs (all, performant, efficient or automatic). Blocked on Intel hybrid CPUs. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/configuration-for-hetero-power-scheduling-schedulingpolicy> |
| `SHORTSCHEDPOLICY` | Hybrid scheduling | Expert | Where short-running threads may run on hybrid CPUs. Blocked on Intel hybrid CPUs. | <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/configuration-for-hetero-power-scheduling-shortschedulingpolicy> |

## Kernel and memory inspector
 value under these keys is listed; documented ones show their meaning and Windows default. Values linked to a catalog item can be changed only through that item; values linked to a rejected entry are explained and never changed.

### Session Manager\kernel

`HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel`

Settings read by the kernel at boot. Most values here are set by Windows itself; the timer-resolution value is the only one iG Windows Tuner catalogues.

| Value | Windows default | Meaning | Link |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` | not set | 1 restores the pre-2004 behaviour where one process's timer-resolution request affects the whole system. | `sched.global-timer-resolution` |
| `ObCaseInsensitive` | 1 | Object names are case-insensitive. 0 is only for POSIX subsystems and breaks normal Windows path handling. |  |
| `DisableTsx` | not set | Intel TSX control used by speculative-execution mitigations. iG Windows Tuner never changes mitigation settings. | `rejected.spectre-mitigations-off` |
| `MitigationOptions` | not set | System-wide exploit protection settings written by Windows Security or Set-ProcessMitigation -System. Change them only through exploit protection. | `sec.exploit-protection-defaults` |
| `MitigationAuditOptions` | not set | Audit-mode counterpart of MitigationOptions (exploit protection). | `sec.exploit-protection-defaults` |

### Session Manager\Memory Management

`HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management`

The memory manager sizes pools and caches dynamically on 64-bit Windows. The page file configuration is the only value iG Windows Tuner changes here (system-managed page file); the classic 'memory tweaks' are explained and rejected.

| Value | Windows default | Meaning | Link |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PagingFiles` | ?:\pagefile.sys | Page file configuration. '?:\pagefile.sys' means a system-managed page file; 'C:\pagefile.sys 4096 8192' a fixed size; an empty list no page file. | `system.pagefile-auto` |
| `ClearPageFileAtShutdown` | 0 | 1 overwrites the page file at shutdown (security policy 'Shutdown: Clear virtual memory pagefile'); shutdowns get slower. |  |
| `DisablePagingExecutive` | 0 | 1 keeps kernel-mode code and drivers in RAM. No measurable benefit with enough memory. | `rejected.disable-paging-executive` |
| `LargeSystemCache` | 0 | 1 favours the file cache over programs, a server setting that hurts desktop responsiveness. | `rejected.large-system-cache` |
| `FeatureSettingsOverride` | not set | Overrides speculative-execution mitigations. Set by tools that turn mitigations off. | `rejected.spectre-mitigations-off` |
| `FeatureSettingsOverrideMask` | not set | Mask that goes with FeatureSettingsOverride. | `rejected.spectre-mitigations-off` |
| `SecondLevelDataCache` | 0 | Legacy L2 cache size hint from the Windows NT era. Modern Windows reads cache sizes from the CPU and ignores tuning here. |  |
| `NonPagedPoolSize` | 0 | 0 lets Windows size the non-paged pool dynamically (64-bit Windows does this well). |  |
| `PagedPoolSize` | 0 | 0 lets Windows size the paged pool dynamically. |  |
| `SystemPages` | 0 | 0 lets Windows size system page table entries dynamically. |  |
| `SessionPoolSize` | 4 | Session pool size in MB, a Windows default. |  |
| `SessionViewSize` | 48 | Session view space in MB, a Windows default. |  |

### PriorityControl

`HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\PriorityControl`

Win32PrioritySeparation controls quantum length and the foreground boost. Windows' client default already favours the foreground window.

| Value | Windows default | Meaning | Link |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Win32PrioritySeparation` | 2 | Quantum length and foreground boost. 2 is the client default (short, variable quanta with foreground boost). | `rejected.win32-priority-separation` |
| `IRQ8Priority` | not set | A Windows 9x-era myth; Windows NT ignores IRQ priority values here. | `rejected.irq-priority` |
| `ConvertibleSlateMode` | 0 | Tablet/laptop posture reported by convertible devices. Not a tuning value. |  |

### Multimedia\SystemProfile (MMCSS)

`HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile`

MMCSS reserves CPU time for low-priority work while multimedia threads run and throttles non-multimedia network processing during playback. Values below 10 or above 100 are clamped to 20 by Windows.

| Value | Windows default | Meaning | Link |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SystemResponsiveness` | 20 | Percentage of CPU guaranteed to low-priority work. Rounded down to tens; below 10 or above 100 is clamped to 20; 100 disables MMCSS. | `sched.system-responsiveness` |
| `NetworkThrottlingIndex` | 10 | Limits non-multimedia network packet processing while MMCSS multimedia playback runs. 0xFFFFFFFF disables the throttling. | `sched.network-throttling-off` |
| `NoLazyMode` | not set | Undocumented community value. Not read by current Windows as far as Microsoft documents. |  |

### MMCSS task: Games

`HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile\Tasks\Games`

Only applies to threads that call the MMCSS API for the Games task; most games do not. Microsoft documents GPU Priority and SFIO Priority as unused, so the popular edits have no effect.

| Value | Windows default | Meaning | Link |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Affinity` | 0 | Processor affinity bitmask; 0 means no affinity. | `rejected.mmcss-games-task` |
| `Background Only` | False | Whether the task has no user interface. | `rejected.mmcss-games-task` |
| `Clock Rate` | 10000 | Scheduling granularity hint (100 ns units); no guarantee since Windows 7. | `rejected.mmcss-games-task` |
| `GPU Priority` | 8 | Documented by Microsoft as not used. | `rejected.mmcss-games-task` |
| `Priority` | 2 | Task priority 1 (low) to 8 (high). | `rejected.mmcss-games-task` |
| `Scheduling Category` | Medium | High, Medium or Low scheduling category. | `rejected.mmcss-games-task` |
| `SFIO Priority` | Normal | Documented by Microsoft as not used. | `rejected.mmcss-games-task` |

### CrashControl

`HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl`

Startup and recovery settings: the dump type, where dumps go, and whether Windows restarts automatically. Changes take effect after a restart.

| Value | Windows default | Meaning | Link |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CrashDumpEnabled` | 7 | 0 none, 1 complete, 2 kernel, 3 small (minidump), 7 automatic memory dump. | `system.dump-small` |
| `AutoReboot` | 1 | 1 restarts automatically after a blue screen; 0 keeps the stop screen up. |  |
| `DumpFile` | %SystemRoot%\MEMORY.DMP | Path of the kernel, complete or automatic memory dump. |  |
| `MinidumpDir` | %SystemRoot%\Minidump | Folder for small memory dumps. |  |
| `Overwrite` | 1 | 1 overwrites an existing memory dump file. |  |
| `LogEvent` | 1 | 1 writes an event to the System log after a stop error. |  |
| `DisplayParameters` | not set | 1 shows the stop code parameters on the blue screen (community-known value, not documented by Microsoft). | `system.bsod-details` |

## Other inspectors

- **Interrupts:** PCI devices with supported interrupt types (line, MSI, MSI-X), the mode in use (from the allocated interrupt resources), MSISupported / MessageNumberLimit, affinity policy, priority and target CPUs. Changes only through `gfx.gpu-msi` (GPU, Expert, reboot); manual affinity pinning is rejected.
- **Network queues:** RSS state, base and max processor, queues, receive and transmit buffers with the driver's range, and discarded-packet counters; advice is based on that evidence.
- **Timer:** GlobalTimerResolutionRequests behaviour (catalog item `sched.global-timer-resolution`). The current timer resolution is not shown because reading it needs an undocumented native call; `powercfg /energy` (administrator) lists timer requests.
- **Crash and page file:** dump type, dump files on disk, stop screen and verbose status settings, page file configuration and usage, with the System catalog items that change them.

```

`docs/README.md`:

```md
# iG Windows Tuner

iG Windows Tuner is an auditable PowerShell + WPF toolbox that tunes **Windows 11 Pro (24H2 / 25H2 / 26H2, builds 26100 / 26200 / 26300)** for competitive online gaming (lower input and network latency, steadier frametimes) while keeping or **raising** security, and without breaking kernel anti-cheat (FACEIT, Riot Vanguard, Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, RICOCHET, Javelin).

Every change is:

1. **Proven**: documented by Microsoft or the vendor (Tier A), or real but situational and marked "measure before/after" (Tier B). Popular placebo tweaks are listed with the reason on the *Rejected Tweaks* page ([REJECTED_TWEAKS.md](REJECTED_TWEAKS.md)).
2. **Reversible**: a JSON snapshot of the exact previous value, including its type and "the value did not exist", is written before anything changes. A System Restore point is created too.
3. **Compatible**: detected at runtime. Nothing that anti-cheat needs (TPM, Secure Boot, VBS, HVCI, IOMMU) is ever touched.
4. **Transparent**: the GUI and `-DryRun` show every registry path and value (current -> target) before applying.

## Requirements

- Windows 11 Pro, build 26100 or newer (older builds are refused).
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 (inbox). PowerShell 7.4+ also works.
- No downloads and no dependencies. Pester and PSScriptAnalyzer are needed only for development.

## Quick start

All read-only commands work without elevation:

```powershell
# Health and anti-cheat readiness report (read-only); optionally save it as HTML
.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Report
.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Report -ReportPath .\report.html

# Every tweak with its tier, risk, presets and current state
.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -ListTweaks

# What a preset would change (prints the full diff, changes nothing)
.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Preset Competitive -DryRun

# GUI (double-click Start-iGWindowsTuner.cmd, or:)
.\Start-iGWindowsTuner.cmd
```

The commands that change the system request elevation through the normal UAC prompt:

```powershell
.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Preset Balanced                 # restore point + snapshot, then apply
.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Apply gfx.windowed-optimizations,input.pointer-precision-off
.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Revert input.pointer-precision-off
.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -RevertAll                       # revert the most recent apply
.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -RevertAll -Snapshot "C:\ProgramData\iGWindowsTuner\Backups\snapshot-....json"
.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -ResetDefault gfx.hags           # documented Windows default
```

Options: `-DryRun`, `-SkipRestorePoint` (the JSON snapshot is still written), `-EnableSystemProtection` (consent to turn on System Protection for C: when it is off), `-AcknowledgeRisk` (required for expert toggles), `-Json` (machine-readable output), `-NoGui`.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | Error |
| 2 | Invalid arguments, unknown tweak id, conflicting selection, or an expert toggle without `-AcknowledgeRisk` |
| 3 | Elevation declined |
| 4 | Preflight refused (build older than 26100, or System Protection off without consent) |
| 5 | One or more tweaks failed and were rolled back |
| 6 | Nothing to revert |
| 3010 | Success; a reboot is required |

## Presets

| Preset | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Competitive** | Every Tier A performance, input and network item, plus the Tier B latency items. The security baseline (Defender, VBS/HVCI, ASR baseline, LSA protection, firewall) stays fully on. |
| **Balanced** | Recommended daily driver: Tier A performance plus Tier A security and privacy. No Tier B. |
| **Hardened** | Balanced plus encrypted DNS (Quad9), AI features off, Office/Adobe ASR rules in Block mode, Controlled Folder Access audit, UAC always-notify, NetBIOS/RDP/Remote Assistance off, PowerShell script block logging, unused Wi-Fi off. Still compatible with competitive anti-cheat. |

The full lists are in [PRESETS.md](PRESETS.md), and every tweak with its exact changes and sources is in [TWEAKS.md](TWEAKS.md). Both are generated from the catalog by `tools\Build-Docs.ps1`.

## GUI

- A dark Windows 11-style window (minimum 1100x720) with icons from the inbox Segoe Fluent Icons font.
- **Header**: hardware summary, OS build, admin badge, and an anti-cheat readiness pill (green, amber or red).
- **Pages**: Dashboard (health), Presets, Power & CPU, Graphics & Display, Input, Network, Background & Privacy, Security, Startup Apps, Backups & Logs, Rejected Tweaks, About.
- **Toggles** always show the real current state. Toggling only stages a change. The bottom bar shows `N pending - Preview - Apply - Discard`, and Preview is a dry-run diff.
- **Details pane**: description, exact changes (current -> target), clickable sources, how to revert, and "reset to Windows default".
- **Search and filters**: text, tier, risk, needs restart, changed from default. Shortcuts: Ctrl+F to search, F5 to refresh.
- **Background work**: all long operations run in a background runspace, so the window never freezes. A collapsible log console shows progress.
- **Read-only start**: the GUI starts read-only. Applying requires "Restart as administrator", which uses the normal UAC prompt.

## What iG Windows Tuner never does

- Edit BCD (there is no `bcdedit` anywhere), enable test signing, disable driver signature enforcement, enable kernel debugging, or disable DEP/ASLR/CFG.
- Touch Secure Boot, TPM, firmware, voltages, power limits or CPU C-states, or install drivers.
- Touch game processes or files, or anti-cheat services (vgc/vgk, FACEIT, EasyAntiCheat, BEService).
- Disable Defender, Tamper Protection, AMSI, ETW, the firewall, UAC, SmartScreen or Windows Update, or add Defender exclusions.
- Create persistence (scheduled tasks, services, Run keys, WMI subscriptions), hide windows, download anything, or change the machine or user execution policy.

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the full engineering rules and [ANTICHEAT.md](ANTICHEAT.md) for anti-cheat requirements.

## Files and folders

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `%ProgramData%\iGWindowsTuner\Backups` | JSON snapshots (one per apply, revert, reset or startup change) |
| `%ProgramData%\iGWindowsTuner\Logs` | `iGWindowsTuner-yyyyMMdd.log` (text) and `.jsonl` (JSON lines). Read-only runs log to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\iGWindowsTuner\Logs` |
| `%ProgramData%\iGWindowsTuner\State` | `pending-restart.json` (drives the restart banner) |
| `%ProgramData%\iGWindowsTuner\Reports` | HTML reports exported from the GUI |

The data folder gets an ACL that grants write access to SYSTEM and Administrators only, so a standard user cannot plant snapshots that an elevated revert would trust.

## Project layout

```
iGWindowsTuner.ps1              entry point (CLI + GUI), elevation relaunch
Start-iGWindowsTuner.cmd        double-click launcher (process-scope execution policy only)
src/                       module: Core (engine, snapshot, restore point, preflight, logging),
                           Actions (one file per action type), Health (read-only checks), Gui (XAML + code)
data/tweaks/*.json         the catalog (single source of truth)
data/presets/*.json        Competitive, Balanced, Hardened
data/games.json            game executables and discovery hints (Dota 2 first)
data/rejected.json         documented but not implemented
data/schema/               JSON schema for tweak files
tests/                     Pester 5 suite (TestRegistry + mocks only)
tools/                     Build-Docs, Test-Catalog, Invoke-QualityChecks, Sign-Toolbox, New-Release,
                           iGWindowsTuner.wsb + Invoke-SandboxTest (Windows Sandbox end-to-end test)
docs/                      this documentation
```

## Troubleshooting

- **"running scripts is disabled"**: use `Start-iGWindowsTuner.cmd`. It passes `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` to that one PowerShell process only.
- **Files downloaded as a zip**: Windows marks them as coming from the internet. Review the files, verify `SHA256SUMS.txt`, then run `Get-ChildItem -Recurse | Unblock-File` if you trust them.
- **A tweak shows "Managed by policy"**: Group Policy or MDM controls that setting, so iG Windows Tuner will not fight it.
- **"Not verified" after apply**: Windows or Tamper Protection refused or rewrote the value. iG Windows Tuner reports it instead of working around it.
- **Undo everything**: Backups & Logs > Revert last apply, or `.\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -RevertAll`. The System Restore point created before each apply is a second safety net.

```

`docs/REJECTED_TWEAKS.md`:

```md
# Rejected tweaks

> Generated by `tools\Build-Docs.ps1` from `data\rejected.json`. Do not edit by hand.

These popular tweaks are deliberately **not implemented**. Each is placebo, obsolete, unstable, security-reducing or hostile to kernel anti-cheat. The only exception is the warned expert toggle `sec.vbs-hvci-off-expert`, which is never part of a preset.

| Tweak | Category | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| BCD timer tweaks (useplatformclock, useplatformtick, disabledynamictick, tscsyncpolicy) | unstable | No consistent measured gain on modern TSC-invariant CPUs; forcing the platform clock often increases timer overhead. Any BCD change can trigger BitLocker recovery, and iG Windows Tuner never runs bcdedit. |
| Disabling HPET in Device Manager or BIOS | placebo | Windows already prefers the invariant TSC; disabling the HPET device changes nothing measurable or breaks software that needs it. |
| Disabling VBS / Memory integrity in a preset | anti-cheat-hostile | FACEIT Anti-Cheat and Riot Vanguard On-Demand require VBS/HVCI, and it removes kernel exploit protection. Available only as the warned expert toggle sec.vbs-hvci-off-expert, never in a preset. |
| Disabling Spectre/Meltdown mitigations (FeatureSettingsOverride) | security-reducing | Removes protection against speculative-execution attacks reachable from browsers and games; gains on Raptor Lake are negligible for games. |
| Win32PrioritySeparation edits | placebo | The default (programs) already boosts the foreground; arbitrary hex values from guides change quantum lengths in ways that were never measured to help and can hurt background audio/voice. |
| Disabling the page file | unstable | Games and drivers reserve commit charge; without a page file, commit can run out with RAM still free, causing crashes. No crash dumps either. |
| Disabling memory compression (32 GB RAM) | placebo | With 32 GB RAM compression rarely runs during play; disabling it only increases paging under pressure. |
| LargeSystemCache = 1 | obsolete | A server-era switch that favors the file cache over application working sets; harmful for games. |
| DisablePagingExecutive = 1 | obsolete | No measurable effect on modern systems with ample RAM. |
| Disabling Fullscreen Optimizations globally | obsolete | Modern flip-model presentation gives exclusive-fullscreen latency in borderless windows; disabling FSO globally can break VRR, Auto HDR and the Game Bar. Per-game compatibility settings remain available in Windows. |
| MouseDataQueueSize / KeyboardDataQueueSize | placebo | Buffer sizes for the legacy class drivers; a smaller queue does not deliver input sooner, it only risks dropped input. |
| IRQ priority registry keys (IRQ8Priority etc.) | placebo | These values are not read by the modern Windows kernel or APIC-based interrupt routing. |
| SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB | security-reducing | Merging services into shared hosts saves trivial memory with 32 GB and removes the isolation and reliability benefit of split service hosts. |
| Power Throttling off on hybrid CPUs | placebo | Power Throttling targets background processes; turning it off lets background work compete for P-cores. iG Windows Tuner instead offers power.power-throttling-on to repair this tweak. |
| E-core disabling, global affinity masks, Thread Director / heterogeneous policy overrides, core parking edits, OS C-state changes | unstable | Thread Director and the Windows scheduler already place foreground threads on P-cores; overriding them removes headroom for background work and can cause stutter. C-states belong to BIOS. |
| Legacy TCP/IP parameters (TcpWindowSize, Tcp1323Opts, DefaultTTL, MaxUserPort, MTU changes) | obsolete | Ignored or superseded by receive-window auto-tuning since Windows Vista; wrong MTU values cause fragmentation and drops. |
| TCP auto-tuning disabled | placebo | Does not reduce game (UDP) latency and caps TCP throughput on fast links. iG Windows Tuner repairs it to Normal instead. |
| TCPNoDelay interface registry value | placebo | Windows TCP does not read this per-interface value; Nagle is a per-socket option (TCP_NODELAY) set by the game. The related TcpAckFrequency setting is offered as net.delayed-ack-off. |
| MMCSS 'Games' task profile (GPU Priority 8, Priority 6, Scheduling Category High, SFIO High) | placebo | Microsoft documents GPU Priority as 'not yet used', SFIO Priority as 'not used', and Priority as always treated as 2 when Scheduling Category is High. Only threads that register with the MMCSS 'Games' task are affected at all, which few games do. |
| NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers | obsolete | Microsoft states the policy does not work exactly as described, applies only with AUOptions = 4, and can prevent quality-update reboots entirely. iG Windows Tuner uses the documented active-hours policy instead (privacy.update-active-hours). |
| TurnOffWindowsCopilot policy | obsolete | Deprecated by Microsoft and not applicable to the current Microsoft Copilot app; RemoveMicrosoftCopilotApp is not supported on Pro. Uninstall the app from Settings instead. |
| System-wide Mandatory ASLR (force randomization for images) | unstable | Forcing relocation of images that were not built for it breaks some games, launchers and anti-cheat components. Per-app exploit protection remains available in Windows Security. |
| Defender exclusions for game folders | security-reducing | Creates a blind spot that malware (including cheat loaders) uses; real-time scanning cost on NVMe is small. iG Windows Tuner never adds exclusions. |
| Disabling Defender, Windows Update, Firewall, UAC, DEP or SmartScreen | security-reducing | Large security loss for negligible performance gain; several kernel anti-cheats and game stores also rely on these components. |
| Feature-flag overrides (ViVeTool, FeatureManagement overrides, native NVMe driver hacks) | unstable | Unsupported, change between builds without notice, and can leave the system in states Microsoft never tested. |
| Removing inbox components with DISM | unstable | Not reversible from inside Windows, breaks servicing and cumulative updates, and some removed components are dependencies of games or anti-cheat. |
| Standby-list cleaners and timer-resolution services | placebo | Windows manages the standby list; purging it discards useful cache. Background services that hold timer resolution raise power use for everyone and need persistence that iG Windows Tuner deliberately avoids. |
| Writing NVIDIA driver profiles (Profile Inspector style) | unstable | Undocumented driver database edits; iG Windows Tuner only shows a read-only checklist for NVIDIA Control Panel and in-game Reflex. |
| Hypervisor launch type off (bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off) | anti-cheat-hostile | Turns off VBS, memory integrity, Windows Hello Enhanced Sign-in Security, WSL2, Windows Sandbox and Hyper-V, and FACEIT and Riot Vanguard On-Demand refuse to run. It is a BCD change, which iG Windows Tuner never makes (BitLocker recovery risk). The warned VBS/HVCI expert toggle covers the measurable part without touching BCD. |
| Processor idle disable (IDLEDISABLE power setting) | unstable | Keeps every core at active voltage and clock all the time: much more heat and power for a latency gain that is not measurable in games on current CPUs. On 13th and 14th gen Intel desktop CPUs it adds to the conditions behind Vmin Shift instability. The power plan editor never offers it and the Raptor Lake overlay blocks it. |
| Pinning device interrupts to specific cores (AssignmentSetOverride) | unstable | Overrides Windows' interrupt steering with a fixed core mask that does not follow hybrid P-core/E-core scheduling, core parking or driver updates; a bad mask can starve a device. The interrupt inspector shows the current policy and target CPUs read-only. |
| Test signing, nointegritychecks, kernel debugging or driver signature enforcement off | anti-cheat-hostile | Removes kernel code-integrity protection. Every kernel anti-cheat refuses to start while any of these is active, and they are BCD changes, which iG Windows Tuner never makes. The health report flags them if they are on. |
| Image File Execution Options edits on game executables (PerfOptions, Debugger) | anti-cheat-hostile | IFEO is a classic hijack location that Microsoft Defender and kernel anti-cheats watch; edits on game executables can be flagged. Raising a game above normal priority does not help when Windows already boosts the foreground window, and can starve audio and input threads. |
| Registry cleaners | unstable | Leftover registry entries do not slow Windows down measurably, and automated deletion breaks applications and uninstallers. The iG Windows Tuner cleaner only deletes files from allow-listed cache folders. |
| Blocking telemetry through the hosts file | security-reducing | Microsoft Defender detects hosts-file entries that block Microsoft endpoints as a settings modifier (HostsFileHijack), and the blocks break Windows Update, activation and Store downloads. iG Windows Tuner uses the documented diagnostic data policies instead. |
| Cleaning the Prefetch folder | placebo | Windows uses the Prefetch traces to load applications faster and rebuilds them anyway, so deleting them only makes the next launches slower. The cleaner never touches %SystemRoot%\Prefetch. |
| Deleting files inside WinSxS or %SystemRoot%\Installer by hand | unstable | WinSxS uses hard links (its real size is much smaller than Explorer shows) and Installer holds the packages needed to repair, update and uninstall software. Manual deletion breaks servicing and uninstallers. The cleaner uses DISM component cleanup instead. |
| Disabling IPv6 | unstable | Microsoft does not support disabling IPv6; components such as Teredo, Xbox networking and some Windows features expect it. When IPv6 causes a problem, Microsoft's guidance is to prefer IPv4 over IPv6 instead. |

## BCD timer tweaks (useplatformclock, useplatformtick, disabledynamictick, tscsyncpolicy)

- **Claim:** Forces HPET/TSC behavior for lower input latency.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** No consistent measured gain on modern TSC-invariant CPUs; forcing the platform clock often increases timer overhead. Any BCD change can trigger BitLocker recovery, and iG Windows Tuner never runs bcdedit.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devtest/bcdedit--set> <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/bitlocker/recovery-overview>

## Disabling HPET in Device Manager or BIOS

- **Claim:** Removes timer latency.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** Windows already prefers the invariant TSC; disabling the HPET device changes nothing measurable or breaks software that needs it.

## Disabling VBS / Memory integrity in a preset

- **Claim:** A few percent more FPS.
- **Category:** anti-cheat-hostile
- **Reason:** FACEIT Anti-Cheat and Riot Vanguard On-Demand require VBS/HVCI, and it removes kernel exploit protection. Available only as the warned expert toggle sec.vbs-hvci-off-expert, never in a preset.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/enable-virtualization-based-protection-of-code-integrity>

## Disabling Spectre/Meltdown mitigations (FeatureSettingsOverride)

- **Claim:** Restores lost CPU performance.
- **Category:** security-reducing
- **Reason:** Removes protection against speculative-execution attacks reachable from browsers and games; gains on Raptor Lake are negligible for games.
- **Sources:** <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/kb4073119-windows-client-guidance-for-it-pros-to-protect-against-silicon-based-microarchitectural-and-speculative-execution-side-channel-vulnerabilities-35820a8a-ae13-1299-88cc-357f104f5b11>

## Win32PrioritySeparation edits

- **Claim:** Gives the foreground game more CPU quantum.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** The default (programs) already boosts the foreground; arbitrary hex values from guides change quantum lengths in ways that were never measured to help and can hurt background audio/voice.

## Disabling the page file

- **Claim:** Avoids disk paging.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** Games and drivers reserve commit charge; without a page file, commit can run out with RAM still free, causing crashes. No crash dumps either.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/performance/how-to-determine-the-appropriate-page-file-size-for-64-bit-versions-of-windows>

## Disabling memory compression (32 GB RAM)

- **Claim:** Saves CPU time.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** With 32 GB RAM compression rarely runs during play; disabling it only increases paging under pressure.

## LargeSystemCache = 1

- **Claim:** Faster file access.
- **Category:** obsolete
- **Reason:** A server-era switch that favors the file cache over application working sets; harmful for games.

## DisablePagingExecutive = 1

- **Claim:** Keeps the kernel in RAM.
- **Category:** obsolete
- **Reason:** No measurable effect on modern systems with ample RAM.

## Disabling Fullscreen Optimizations globally

- **Claim:** Restores true exclusive fullscreen.
- **Category:** obsolete
- **Reason:** Modern flip-model presentation gives exclusive-fullscreen latency in borderless windows; disabling FSO globally can break VRR, Auto HDR and the Game Bar. Per-game compatibility settings remain available in Windows.
- **Sources:** <https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/3f006843-2c7e-4ed0-9a5e-f9389e535952>

## MouseDataQueueSize / KeyboardDataQueueSize

- **Claim:** Lower input latency.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** Buffer sizes for the legacy class drivers; a smaller queue does not deliver input sooner, it only risks dropped input.

## IRQ priority registry keys (IRQ8Priority etc.)

- **Claim:** Prioritizes the timer or GPU interrupt.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** These values are not read by the modern Windows kernel or APIC-based interrupt routing.

## SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB

- **Claim:** Fewer svchost processes, less overhead.
- **Category:** security-reducing
- **Reason:** Merging services into shared hosts saves trivial memory with 32 GB and removes the isolation and reliability benefit of split service hosts.

## Power Throttling off on hybrid CPUs

- **Claim:** Prevents throttling of the game.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** Power Throttling targets background processes; turning it off lets background work compete for P-cores. iG Windows Tuner instead offers power.power-throttling-on to repair this tweak.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/quality-of-service>

## E-core disabling, global affinity masks, Thread Director / heterogeneous policy overrides, core parking edits, OS C-state changes

- **Claim:** Keeps the game on P-cores.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** Thread Director and the Windows scheduler already place foreground threads on P-cores; overriding them removes headroom for background work and can cause stutter. C-states belong to BIOS.

## Legacy TCP/IP parameters (TcpWindowSize, Tcp1323Opts, DefaultTTL, MaxUserPort, MTU changes)

- **Claim:** Faster or lower-latency networking.
- **Category:** obsolete
- **Reason:** Ignored or superseded by receive-window auto-tuning since Windows Vista; wrong MTU values cause fragmentation and drops.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/technologies/network-subsystem/net-sub-performance-tuning-nics>

## TCP auto-tuning disabled

- **Claim:** Lower ping.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** Does not reduce game (UDP) latency and caps TCP throughput on fast links. iG Windows Tuner repairs it to Normal instead.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/nettcpip/set-nettcpsetting>

## TCPNoDelay interface registry value

- **Claim:** Disables Nagle's algorithm system-wide.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** Windows TCP does not read this per-interface value; Nagle is a per-socket option (TCP_NODELAY) set by the game. The related TcpAckFrequency setting is offered as net.delayed-ack-off.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winsock/ipproto-tcp-socket-options>

## MMCSS 'Games' task profile (GPU Priority 8, Priority 6, Scheduling Category High, SFIO High)

- **Claim:** Higher priority for game threads.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** Microsoft documents GPU Priority as 'not yet used', SFIO Priority as 'not used', and Priority as always treated as 2 when Scheduling Category is High. Only threads that register with the MMCSS 'Games' task are affected at all, which few games do.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/multimedia-class-scheduler-service>

## NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers

- **Claim:** Windows Update never restarts while you are signed in.
- **Category:** obsolete
- **Reason:** Microsoft states the policy does not work exactly as described, applies only with AUOptions = 4, and can prevent quality-update reboots entirely. iG Windows Tuner uses the documented active-hours policy instead (privacy.update-active-hours).
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/update/waas-restart>

## TurnOffWindowsCopilot policy

- **Claim:** Removes Copilot.
- **Category:** obsolete
- **Reason:** Deprecated by Microsoft and not applicable to the current Microsoft Copilot app; RemoveMicrosoftCopilotApp is not supported on Pro. Uninstall the app from Settings instead.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-windowsai>

## System-wide Mandatory ASLR (force randomization for images)

- **Claim:** Extra exploit protection.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** Forcing relocation of images that were not built for it breaks some games, launchers and anti-cheat components. Per-app exploit protection remains available in Windows Security.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/exploit-protection-reference>

## Defender exclusions for game folders

- **Claim:** Faster loading.
- **Category:** security-reducing
- **Reason:** Creates a blind spot that malware (including cheat loaders) uses; real-time scanning cost on NVMe is small. iG Windows Tuner never adds exclusions.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/common-exclusion-mistakes-microsoft-defender-antivirus>

## Disabling Defender, Windows Update, Firewall, UAC, DEP or SmartScreen

- **Claim:** Less background overhead.
- **Category:** security-reducing
- **Reason:** Large security loss for negligible performance gain; several kernel anti-cheats and game stores also rely on these components.

## Feature-flag overrides (ViVeTool, FeatureManagement overrides, native NVMe driver hacks)

- **Claim:** Unlocks hidden performance features.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** Unsupported, change between builds without notice, and can leave the system in states Microsoft never tested.

## Removing inbox components with DISM

- **Claim:** Debloats Windows.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** Not reversible from inside Windows, breaks servicing and cumulative updates, and some removed components are dependencies of games or anti-cheat.

## Standby-list cleaners and timer-resolution services

- **Claim:** Fixes stutter.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** Windows manages the standby list; purging it discards useful cache. Background services that hold timer resolution raise power use for everyone and need persistence that iG Windows Tuner deliberately avoids.

## Writing NVIDIA driver profiles (Profile Inspector style)

- **Claim:** Forces low-latency driver settings.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** Undocumented driver database edits; iG Windows Tuner only shows a read-only checklist for NVIDIA Control Panel and in-game Reflex.

## Hypervisor launch type off (bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off)

- **Claim:** Removes virtualization overhead for more FPS.
- **Category:** anti-cheat-hostile
- **Reason:** Turns off VBS, memory integrity, Windows Hello Enhanced Sign-in Security, WSL2, Windows Sandbox and Hyper-V, and FACEIT and Riot Vanguard On-Demand refuse to run. It is a BCD change, which iG Windows Tuner never makes (BitLocker recovery risk). The warned VBS/HVCI expert toggle covers the measurable part without touching BCD.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/enable-virtualization-based-protection-of-code-integrity>

## Processor idle disable (IDLEDISABLE power setting)

- **Claim:** Removes C-state wake-up latency.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** Keeps every core at active voltage and clock all the time: much more heat and power for a latency gain that is not measurable in games on current CPUs. On 13th and 14th gen Intel desktop CPUs it adds to the conditions behind Vmin Shift instability. The power plan editor never offers it and the Raptor Lake overlay blocks it.
- **Sources:** <https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000102331/processors.html>

## Pinning device interrupts to specific cores (AssignmentSetOverride)

- **Claim:** Moves GPU or NIC interrupts off busy cores for lower latency.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** Overrides Windows' interrupt steering with a fixed core mask that does not follow hybrid P-core/E-core scheduling, core parking or driver updates; a bad mask can starve a device. The interrupt inspector shows the current policy and target CPUs read-only.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/kernel/interrupt-affinity-and-priority>

## Test signing, nointegritychecks, kernel debugging or driver signature enforcement off

- **Claim:** Lets you load unsigned tuning drivers.
- **Category:** anti-cheat-hostile
- **Reason:** Removes kernel code-integrity protection. Every kernel anti-cheat refuses to start while any of these is active, and they are BCD changes, which iG Windows Tuner never makes. The health report flags them if they are on.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/install/the-testsigning-boot-configuration-option>

## Image File Execution Options edits on game executables (PerfOptions, Debugger)

- **Claim:** Forces high CPU or I/O priority for a game on every launch.
- **Category:** anti-cheat-hostile
- **Reason:** IFEO is a classic hijack location that Microsoft Defender and kernel anti-cheats watch; edits on game executables can be flagged. Raising a game above normal priority does not help when Windows already boosts the foreground window, and can starve audio and input threads.

## Registry cleaners

- **Claim:** Removes registry junk to speed Windows up.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** Leftover registry entries do not slow Windows down measurably, and automated deletion breaks applications and uninstallers. The iG Windows Tuner cleaner only deletes files from allow-listed cache folders.

## Blocking telemetry through the hosts file

- **Claim:** Stops Windows from sending data.
- **Category:** security-reducing
- **Reason:** Microsoft Defender detects hosts-file entries that block Microsoft endpoints as a settings modifier (HostsFileHijack), and the blocks break Windows Update, activation and Store downloads. iG Windows Tuner uses the documented diagnostic data policies instead.

## Cleaning the Prefetch folder

- **Claim:** Speeds up application launches.
- **Category:** placebo
- **Reason:** Windows uses the Prefetch traces to load applications faster and rebuilds them anyway, so deleting them only makes the next launches slower. The cleaner never touches %SystemRoot%\Prefetch.

## Deleting files inside WinSxS or %SystemRoot%\Installer by hand

- **Claim:** Frees many gigabytes.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** WinSxS uses hard links (its real size is much smaller than Explorer shows) and Installer holds the packages needed to repair, update and uninstall software. Manual deletion breaks servicing and uninstallers. The cleaner uses DISM component cleanup instead.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/clean-up-the-winsxs-folder>

## Disabling IPv6

- **Claim:** Lowers latency and fixes connection problems.
- **Category:** unstable
- **Reason:** Microsoft does not support disabling IPv6; components such as Teredo, Xbox networking and some Windows features expect it. When IPv6 causes a problem, Microsoft's guidance is to prefer IPv4 over IPv6 instead.
- **Sources:** <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/networking/configure-ipv6-in-windows>


```

`docs/SCHEMA.md`:

```md
# Data schema v2

iG Windows Tuner 2.0 data files declare `"schemaVersion": 2`. JSON Schema documents for editors are in
`data\schema\` (`tweak.schema.json`, `preset.schema.json`, `cleaner-rule.schema.json`); the
authoritative checks are `Test-IgwtCatalog` and `Test-IgwtCleanerCatalog`, which the Pester
suite runs.

## Fields shared by every item

Every user-facing item (tweak, cleaner rule, preset, hardware tag) has:

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `hint` | Tooltip, 140 characters or fewer. |
| `description` | What it does, why, the trade-off and how to revert (at least 40 characters). |

Tweaks and cleaner rules also have:

| Field | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `level` | `Standard`, `Advanced`, `Expert`, `Lab` | Who should use the item and how it is gated. Separate from the evidence tier. |
| tier | `A`, `B` | Evidence tier: `evidence.tier` for tweaks, top-level `tier` for cleaner rules. Rejected ideas live in `data\rejected.json`. |
| `antiCheat` | `"safe"`, `"unknown"`, `{ "breaks": ["FACEIT", ...] }` | Anything other than `safe` is shown as a badge and kept out of gaming presets. `breaks` requires level `Lab`; `unknown` requires `Expert` or `Lab`. |
| `reversible` | `full`, `partial`, `none` | `full`: the snapshot restores everything. Anything else must be explained in `sideEffects`. Cleaner deletions are `none` (Recycle Bin rules `partial`). |
| `sideEffects` | text | Empty when there are none. |
| `source` | `igwt`, `winutil`, `microsoft` | `winutil` items need an `attribution`. |
| `hardware` | `{ "tags": [], "excludeTags": [] }` | Tags from `data\hardware\tags.json`. Empty until the hardware profile engine (phase 2) assigns them. |

### Levels

| Level | Audience | Gate today | In presets |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | Everyone | none | yes |
| Advanced | Power users | none (mode switch arrives with the GUI restructure) | yes |
| Expert | Engineers | `-AcknowledgeRisk` / GUI confirmation | only inside hardware overlays and the Engineer preset |
| Lab | Benchmarking and research | `-AcknowledgeRisk` / GUI confirmation (typed confirmation and red banner arrive with the GUI restructure) | never |

## Tweak-only fields

`requires` (`none`, `logoff`, `reboot`), `appliesTo` (`minBuild`, optional `maxBuild`,
`editions`, and `conditions`: runtime checks `wiredAdapter`, `multipleGpus`, `nvidiaGpu`,
`defenderActive`, `notRdp`), `warning` (required for Expert and Lab), `impact`, `risk`,
`evidence`, `conflictsWith`, `policyKeys`, `postApply`, `revertNote`, `actions`.

Action definitions did not change from v1. Snapshots match actions by fingerprint (type plus
identifying fields such as path, name and item), so never change those fields on an existing
action; add a new action or a new tweak instead.

### 2.0 action types

| Type | Key fields |
|---|---|
| `storageSense` | `setting` (enabled, cadence, temporaryFiles, recycleBinDays, downloadsDays), `value` |
| `wufbPolicy` | `setting` (featureDeferralDays 0-365, qualityDeferralDays 0-30, targetRelease `{ product, version }`), `value` |
| `deviceInterrupt` | `deviceClass` (Display, Net, USB), any of `msiSupported`, `messageNumberLimit`, `devicePolicy`, `devicePriority`; Expert/Lab, `requires: reboot` |
| `serviceSet` | `services: [{ name, startupType, default }]`, optional `stop` |
| `powercfgAttribute` | `subgroup`, `setting`, `visible`, `default` (hidden or visible), `label` |
| `powercfgSettingAcDc` | `subgroup`, `setting`, `ac`, `dc`, `defaultAc`/`defaultDc` or `defaultFromScheme`, `label` |
| `scheduledTask` | `path` (`\...\`), `name`, `on`/`default` (Enabled, Disabled) |
| `firewallRule` | owned: `rule` (`iGWindowsTuner-*`), `displayName`, `direction`, `action: Block`, optional `protocol`, `localPort`, `remotePort`, `program`, `profile`; or group: `displayGroup`, optional `direction`, `on: Disabled`, `default` |
| `appx` | `package`, `on: Removed`, `default: Installed`, optional `provisioned`, `storeId`; reversible partial |
| `winget` | `id`, optional `source` (winget, msstore), `on`/`default` (Installed, NotInstalled) |
| `capability` | `name`, `on`/`default` (Installed, NotPresent) |
| `processMitigation` | `process` (`name.exe`), `mitigation`, `on` (ON, OFF; OFF needs Expert/Lab) |
| `exploitSystem` | `mitigation`, `on: ON` |
| `cleanerRule` | `rule` (cleaner rule id); reversible none |
| `check` + `checker: DefaultApp` | `extension` or `protocol`, `progId` (read-only) |

## Presets (intent presets)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `include` | Tweak ids in the preset. |
| `exclude` | Ids explicitly kept out, even when a hardware overlay would add them. |
| `levelCeiling` | Highest item level allowed (`Standard`, `Advanced`, `Expert`); Lab is never allowed. |
| `antiCheatPolicy` | `safeOnly` (required for gaming presets) or `any`. |
| `gaming` | Gaming presets may only contain `antiCheat: "safe"` items. |
| `hint`, `description`, `tagline`, `order` | Texts and sort order. |

In memory, every preset also has `tweaks` = `include` minus `exclude`. Phase 2 resolves it
further through the hardware overlays.

## Other data files

| File | Content | Validated by |
|---|---|---|
| `data\asr\rules.json` | The 19 ASR rules: GUID, key, texts, gamer impact, Warn/cloud/server-only flags, recommended mode, sources (`docs\ASR_CENTER.md`). | `Test-IgwtAsrCatalog` |
| `data\power\processor.json` | Processor settings the power plan editor may change: alias, GUID, group, level, texts, sources (`docs\INSPECTORS.md`). | `Test-IgwtPowerSettingCatalog` |
| `data\inspectors\kernel.json` | Registry keys and documented values for the kernel and memory inspector: default, meaning, catalog item or rejected entry. | `Test-IgwtKernelInspectorCatalog` |
| `data\manage\services.json` | Services the management module never changes: groups of `names` and/or wildcard `patterns`, each with a `reason` (200 characters or fewer). | `Test-IgwtManageCatalog` (also requires the spec section 12 core list) |
| `data\manage\nic-keywords.json` | Descriptions of standardized NDIS adapter keywords (`keyword` starting with `*`, `description` of 240 characters or fewer) and the https `source`. | `Test-IgwtManageCatalog` |
| `data\hardware\*.json` | Hardware tags, detection rules and overlays (`docs\HARDWARE.md`). | `Test-IgwtHardwareCatalog` |

All of them run inside `Test-IgwtCatalog`.

## Snapshots

New snapshots are schema 2: `catalogSchema`, `hardwareTags` and a `level` on every entry (so a Lab
item that is still applied can be found). Schema 1 snapshots (iG Windows Tuner 1.x) are read directly and
upgraded in memory; the file is never rewritten. Unknown schemas are refused.

Special operations have their own restore code in `Invoke-IgwtRevert`: `Startup` (StartupApproved),
`ASR` (ASR Center), `Power` (power plan editor) and `Manage` (management modules). A `Manage` entry's
action carries `managed: { kind, target, value, provisioned }`; on revert the action is rebuilt from
those fields and validated again against the protection rules, and only the restore `data` comes
from the file.

## Migration

- **Automatic:** the loaders upgrade v1 tweaks, presets, cleaner rules and snapshots in memory, so
  an old data folder or backup keeps working. `Test-IgwtCatalog` still reports v1 files so they get
  converted.
- **Tool:** `tools\Convert-IgwtV1Data.ps1 [-DataFolder <path>] [-WhatIf]` rewrites v1 files in place
  (idempotent). `-SnapshotFolder <dir> -SnapshotDestination <other dir>` writes schema 2 copies of
  snapshots; originals are never modified.
- **Mapping:** level = Lab for v1 expert items that were not anti-cheat safe, Expert for other v1
  expert items, Advanced for Tier B or medium/high risk, otherwise Standard. `antiCheatSafe: true`
  becomes `"safe"`; `false` becomes `{ "breaks": [...] }` with the anti-cheats named in the warning
  (or `"unknown"`). `appliesTo.hardware` checks move to `appliesTo.conditions`. v1 presets become
  intent presets with `levelCeiling: Advanced` and `antiCheatPolicy: safeOnly`.
- **Renamed ids:** `data\migration\id-map.json` maps old ids to new ones for snapshots and presets.

`docs/SECURITY.md`:

```md
# Security design

iG Windows Tuner runs with administrator rights and edits system settings, so it is written to be as easy to audit as possible, and to look to Microsoft Defender and SmartScreen like what it is: an ordinary, transparent admin script. That is achieved through transparency, never through evasion.

## Engineering rules (all enforced or tested)

| Rule | How |
|---|---|
| Plain, readable source with comment-based help | Every function has help. There is no obfuscation, no Base64 or `-EncodedCommand`, no `Invoke-Expression`, and no command names built from strings. The GUI worker uses `AddCommand` with fixed command names, never `AddScript`. `tests\Safety.Tests.ps1` scans for all of these. |
| Fully offline | Nothing is downloaded at runtime: no `Invoke-WebRequest`, `WebClient` or BITS. |
| No security tampering | No AMSI, ETW, real-time protection, Tamper Protection or exclusion changes. Defender preferences are limited to an allow-list (PUA, MAPS, sample submission, network protection, Controlled Folder Access, scan idle/CPU) and none of them lowers protection. Tamper Protection is read, never changed. |
| No hidden windows and no persistence | No `-WindowStyle Hidden`, scheduled tasks, services, Run keys or WMI subscriptions. The "pending restart" banner is a JSON file that iG Windows Tuner reads when it starts; nothing runs at logon. |
| Visible elevation only | `Start-Process -Verb RunAs` with the normal UAC prompt (`src\Core\Elevation.ps1`). No UAC bypass. The GUI and read-only modes run without elevation. |
| Execution policy | The machine and user policies are never changed. `Start-iGWindowsTuner.cmd` and the elevation relaunch pass `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` to that one process only. |
| Native APIs first | The .NET `Microsoft.Win32.RegistryKey` API is used for all registry work (exact types; `REG_EXPAND_SZ` stays unexpanded), plus inbox cmdlets for Defender, NetAdapter, NetQos, DnsClient, services and firewall. No `reg.exe`, `sc.exe` or `netsh`. |
| Allowed external executables | `powercfg.exe` (power plans), `nvidia-smi.exe` (read-only `-q` / `--query-gpu` only, checked in code), and `MpCmdRun.exe` (build-time scan in `tools\` only). |
| One P/Invoke | A single `Add-Type` with C# source in `src\Actions\Custom.ps1` declares `SystemParametersInfo`. It applies the mouse, key-repeat and accessibility-hotkey settings to the running session and broadcasts `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`. `Add-Type -AssemblyName` is used only to load the inbox WPF assemblies. |
| Packaging | Shipped as `.ps1/.psm1/.psd1/.json/.xaml` plus a `.cmd` launcher. Never an EXE (ps2exe output is frequently flagged). |
| Honest names | Nothing is called "bypass", "stealth" or "kill". |

## Integrity of backups (snapshot trust)

A revert writes values back with administrator rights, so the snapshot files are part of the trusted computing base:

- When elevated, `%ProgramData%\iGWindowsTuner` gets a protected ACL: SYSTEM and Administrators have full control, Users have read access, and inheritance is disabled (`Protect-IgwtDataRoot`).
- Before restoring, `Read-IgwtSnapshot` refuses any file that is not owned by SYSTEM, Administrators, TrustedInstaller or the current elevated user, or that grants write access to Everyone, Authenticated Users, Users, Interactive or Guests.
- **Paths always come from the catalog, never from the snapshot file.** A snapshot only supplies previous values, and each entry is matched to the current catalog action by a fingerprint (type + path + name + ...). If the catalog changed since the snapshot, that entry is not restored and is reported instead.
- Restores for dynamic targets are validated as well: QoS policy names must match the `iGWindowsTuner-<game>` targets, startup entries must belong to the five StartupApproved keys, per-game GPU entries must be `X:\...\*.exe` values under `UserGpuPreferences`, and firewall and TCP values must belong to fixed enumerations.

## Change safety

- **Preflight**: refuses builds older than 26100 and requires admin to apply. It warns when the edition is not Pro, a reboot is pending, a battery is present, or the session is a Remote Desktop session.
- **Remote Desktop**: tweaks that could cut off the connection (Remote Desktop/Assistance off, Wi-Fi disable, DNS changes) report NotApplicable in an RDP session. Adapter property changes use `-NoRestart`, so the link never drops mid-apply.
- **Atomic per tweak**: the snapshot entry is written before the first change. If any action fails, that tweak's already-applied actions are restored, the failure is logged, and the run continues.
- **Idempotent**: tweaks already in the target state are skipped, and actions skip values already in place. A second apply writes nothing.
- **Verification**: after apply, the real state is read again. If Tamper Protection, Group Policy or Windows refused a change, it is reported as "not verified" instead of being worked around.
- **Group Policy and MDM**: tweaks controlled by a policy value show "Managed by policy" and are not applied.
- **Restore point**: one is created before every apply through the WMI `SystemRestore` class. The 24-hour limit is lifted only during that call (`SystemRestorePointCreationFrequency = 0`, then the exact previous value is restored). System Protection is enabled only with explicit consent (GUI dialog or `-EnableSystemProtection`).
- **Over-the-shoulder elevation**: if UAC credentials of a different admin are used, per-user (HKCU) settings are redirected to the signed-in user's hive (`HKEY_USERS\<SID>`), so they apply to the gamer and not to the admin account.
- **Logs**: human-readable text plus JSON lines, in an admin-only folder.

## Code signing (optional)

`tools\Sign-Toolbox.ps1` signs the PowerShell files with **your** code-signing certificate. With `-CreateSelfSignedCertificate` and an explicit confirmation, it creates one in `Cert:\CurrentUser\My`; it never adds it to the trusted stores. The script always writes `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and `-Verify` checks the files against it.

## Reporting a problem

If iG Windows Tuner changed something it should not have, open **Backups & Logs**: every change is in a JSON snapshot and in `%ProgramData%\iGWindowsTuner\Logs`. `-RevertAll -Snapshot <file>` restores any snapshot. The System Restore point created before each apply is a second line of defense.

## End-to-end test in Windows Sandbox (you run this)

Windows Sandbox is a disposable VM, so the real apply/revert path can be exercised there without touching your PC.

1. Enable the optional feature "Windows Sandbox" if it is not on yet (your decision; iG Windows Tuner does not do it).
2. Run `.\tools\New-SandboxConfig.ps1`. It creates `..\iGWindowsTuner-SandboxResults` and writes `tools\iGWindowsTuner.wsb` with this folder's path (the project is mapped read-only).
3. Double-click `tools\iGWindowsTuner.wsb`. At logon the sandbox runs `tools\Invoke-SandboxTest.ps1`, which refuses to run anywhere except the sandbox account. It runs the health report, then applies every non-expert tweak (one of each conflicting pair, no restore point because the sandbox has no System Protection), verifies them, reverts from the snapshot, and verifies that every captured registry value is back exactly.
4. Read `iGWindowsTuner-SandboxResults\summary.txt` (plus `results.json`, `report.html`, `transcript.txt` and the logs).

Expected in the sandbox: GPU, TPM, Secure Boot, HVCI and wired-adapter items report NotApplicable or stay Off (the sandbox has a virtual Hyper-V adapter and no TPM). Defender items depend on the sandbox's Defender state. "PASS" means no apply failures, no revert failures, and no registry value that differs after the revert.

## Manual before/after measurement plan (Tier B items and presets)

Measure on a quiet system (reboot first, close overlays and launchers you do not need), with the same game build, map, settings and replay. Change one thing at a time.

1. **Frametimes**: capture 3 runs of 60-120 s with **PresentMon** (<https://github.com/GameTechDev/PresentMon>) or **CapFrameX**. Compare average FPS, **1 % and 0.1 % lows** and the frametime variance. Dota 2: replay the same demo tick range with `demo_timescale 1`. CS2: a workshop benchmark map. Treat differences inside the run-to-run spread as noise.
2. **Input and system latency**: if the game supports Reflex, read the NVIDIA overlay's PC latency (or use a Reflex Latency Analyzer monitor).
3. **DPC/ISR latency**: run **LatencyMon** for 10 minutes idle and 10 minutes in game. Check the highest DPC/ISR execution time and the driver that caused it, especially after `net.interrupt-moderation-off` and HAGS changes.
4. **Network**: ping and jitter to the game region (the in-game net graph, `ping -n 100 <server>`). Run a **bufferbloat test** (<https://www.waveform.com/tools/bufferbloat>) idle and under load. QoS/DSCP can only help if the router honors DSCP or runs SQM.
5. **Audio**: with SystemResponsiveness 10, listen for crackles under load. MMCSS reserves less CPU for background work.

Record the results (date, build, driver, settings, numbers) next to the snapshot file so any change can be correlated and reverted.

## DPI and layout

- Windows scaling at 100/125/150 %: WPF scales vector content at the system DPI. Every page was rendered at 1.0, 1.25 and 1.5 scale offscreen (`Show-IgwtGui -RenderTo .\shots -Scale 1.25`) and checked for clipping.
- For a real per-monitor check, move the window between monitors with different scaling. It stays sharp on the primary monitor and is bitmap-scaled on others (see DECISIONS E7).
- Keyboard: Tab through the navigation and lists, Space toggles, Ctrl+F searches, F5 refreshes.

# iG Windows Tuner tweak catalog

### High performance power plan

`power.high-performance-plan` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance low, latency low, security 0

*Activates the built-in High performance plan (faster clock ramp-up than Balanced). Slightly higher idle power.*

Makes the inbox High performance scheme (8c5e7fda-...) active. Compared with Balanced, the CPU ramps clocks up faster and devices idle less aggressively. Thread Director and the Windows scheduler still decide which cores run your game. Trade-off: slightly higher idle power.

**Changes**

- Activate power scheme `8c5e7fda-e8bf-4a96-9a85-a6e23a8c635c` (revert re-activates the previous scheme)

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options>

*Evidence notes:* Inbox power scheme.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default power scheme: Balanced.

### Ultimate Performance power plan

`power.ultimate-plan` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance low, latency low, security 0

*Activates the Ultimate Performance plan (High performance minus remaining power-saving timers). Raises idle power. Measure.*

Duplicates the hidden Ultimate Performance scheme (e9a42b02-...) once, or reuses a copy that already exists, and makes it the active plan. Microsoft built it for high-end desktops to eliminate micro-latencies from fine-grained power management. CPU C-states and turbo remain under BIOS control. Trade-off: higher idle power and heat; the gain over High performance is small, so measure frametimes before and after.

**Changes**

- Duplicate `e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61` (or reuse an existing Ultimate copy) and activate it; revert re-activates the previous plan and deletes only a copy iG Windows Tuner created

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options>

*Evidence notes:* Inbox Microsoft scheme (resource text: 'Provides ultimate performance on higher end PCs'), duplicated with the documented powercfg /duplicatescheme. Microsoft's 2018 announcement post is no longer online, so it is Tier B. iG Windows Tuner never changes C-state or processor power settings inside the plan.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Revert re-activates your previous plan and deletes the Ultimate copy only if iG Windows Tuner created it.

### Show hidden processor power settings in Power Options

`power.show-processor-settings` | Advanced | Tier A | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security 0

*Makes 14 hidden processor settings (EPP, boost mode, core parking, idle thresholds, hybrid scheduling) visible in Power Options.*

Clears the hidden attribute (powercfg -attributes ... -ATTRIB_HIDE) of the processor settings that the iG Windows Tuner power plan editor covers, so they also appear under Control Panel > Power Options > Advanced settings. Nothing about how the CPU behaves changes; turning the item off hides them again. Settings that a hardware overlay blocks stay visible but should be left at their defaults.

**Changes**

### PCI Express Link State Power Management off

`power.pcie-aspm-off` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency low, security 0

*Keeps PCIe links (GPU, NVMe, NIC) at full power instead of entering low-power states on AC power.*

Sets the active plan's PCI Express 'Link State Power Management' (ASPM) to Off on AC power. ASPM saves power by putting idle PCIe links into L0s/L1, and waking them adds latency. Trade-off: a few watts of idle power. BIOS ASPM settings still apply.

**Changes**

*Evidence notes:* SUB_PCIEXPRESS 501a4d13-42af-4429-9fd1-a8218c268e20 / ASPM ee12f906-d277-404b-b6da-e5fa1a576df5.

### USB selective suspend off

`power.usb-selective-suspend-off` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency low, security 0

### Fast Startup off

`power.fast-startup-off` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security 0

*Shutdown performs a full kernel and driver restart instead of hibernating the kernel session.*

Sets HiberbootEnabled to 0. With Fast Startup, 'Shut down' hibernates the kernel session, so drivers and the kernel are never freshly initialized until a Restart. Turning it off gives a clean driver state at every boot and avoids stale driver issues. Trade-off: cold boots take a few seconds longer.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Power\HiberbootEnabled` = `0` (DWord); Windows default `1`; absent means `1`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/kernel/distinguishing-fast-startup-from-wake-from-hibernation>

*Evidence notes:* When hibernation is disabled, Fast Startup is unavailable anyway; the value is still set for consistency.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Power\HiberbootEnabled: 1.

### Hibernation off

`power.hibernation-off` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security 0

*Turns off hibernation and deletes hiberfil.sys. Nothing to measure: it frees disk space, not FPS. Only if you never hibernate.*

Runs powercfg /hibernate off, which removes hiberfil.sys (often several GB) and also disables Fast Startup. This is a disk-space and boot-consistency change, not a performance change, so there is nothing to measure before/after. Do not use it if you rely on Hibernate.

**Changes**

*Evidence notes:* Situational: only useful when hibernation is unused.

### Keep Power Throttling on (hybrid CPU)

`power.power-throttling-on` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance low, latency low, security 0

*Removes the 'PowerThrottlingOff' override some tools set. Throttling moves background work to E-cores, away from your game.*

Ensures HKLM\...\Power\PowerThrottling\PowerThrottlingOff is not set to 1. On hybrid Intel CPUs, Power Throttling (EcoQoS) lets Windows and Thread Director steer background processes onto efficiency cores, leaving performance cores to the foreground game. Disabling it is a popular but counter-productive tweak.

**Changes**

*Evidence notes:* Repair-only: value absent (the Windows default) or 0 counts as on.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\PowerThrottling\PowerThrottlingOff: <absent>.

### MMCSS network throttling off

`sched.network-throttling-off` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency low, security 0

*Disables the legacy MMCSS packet-processing limit used during media playback. Measure ping and frametimes before/after.*

Sets NetworkThrottlingIndex to 0xFFFFFFFF. Since Windows Vista, MMCSS can limit non-multimedia network packet processing while multimedia playback is active (default 10 packets per millisecond). Disabling it can help when audio runs alongside online games. It is a legacy mechanism with situational benefit; measure before/after.

*Evidence notes:* Value lives in the documented MMCSS SystemProfile key; its effect is legacy and situational.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile\NetworkThrottlingIndex: 10.

### MMCSS SystemResponsiveness 10%

`sched.system-responsiveness` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance low, latency low, security 0

*Lowers the CPU share MMCSS reserves for background tasks from 20% to 10% (the documented minimum). Measure before/after.*

Sets SystemResponsiveness to 10. The Multimedia Class Scheduler reserves this percentage of CPU for low-priority work while MMCSS-registered threads (audio, some games) run. Microsoft documents that values below 10 are clamped to 20, so 10 is the lowest effective value. Only affects threads registered with MMCSS; measure frametimes and audio before/after.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile\SystemResponsiveness` = `10` (DWord); Windows default `20`; absent means `20`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/multimedia-class-scheduler-service>

*Evidence notes:* Microsoft: values not divisible by 10 are rounded down; values below 10 or above 100 are clamped to 20; 100 disables MMCSS. Corrected from common advice to use 0.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile\SystemResponsiveness: 20.

### Global timer resolution requests (expert)

`sched.global-timer-resolution` | Expert | Tier B | risk medium | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency low, security 0

> **Warning:** Raises idle power and timer interrupt rate for the whole system. Games already request their own timer resolution, so most players gain nothing.

*Restores pre-2004 behavior where one app's timer request applies system-wide. Raises idle power. Measure before/after.*

Sets GlobalTimerResolutionRequests to 1. Since Windows 10 2004 a process's timeBeginPeriod request only affects that process, and Windows 11 ignores requests from minimized or fully occluded windows. Games set their own timer resolution, so this only matters for tools that depend on another process's request. Trade-off: more timer interrupts and higher idle power. Measure before/after.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel\GlobalTimerResolutionRequests` = `1` (DWord); Windows default `<absent>`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/timeapi/nf-timeapi-timebeginperiod>
- <https://randomascii.wordpress.com/2020/10/04/windows-timer-resolution-the-great-rule-change/>

*Evidence notes:* Registry value is honored on Windows 11 and Server 2022+, measured and documented by Bruce Dawson; not a BCD change.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel\GlobalTimerResolutionRequests: <absent>.

### Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling

### GPU message-signaled interrupts (MSI)

`gfx.gpu-msi` | Expert | Tier B | risk medium | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency low, security 0

> **Warning:** Changes how the graphics card signals interrupts. Takes effect after a reboot. If the screen stays black or flickers after the reboot, start in Safe Mode or use another display output and revert this item.

*EXPERT: switches the GPU to MSI where its driver declares support. Many GPUs already use MSI. Reboot; measure DPC latency.*

Sets MSISupported = 1 under the GPU's Interrupt Management key, but only when its driver declares MSI support. Message-signaled interrupts avoid shared interrupt lines and can lower interrupt latency; most current GPUs already use them, and the interrupt inspector shows the mode in use. Measure DPC latency (LatencyMon) before and after. If the display misbehaves after the reboot, revert from Backups & Logs.

**Changes**

- Interrupt settings msiSupported=1 of present PCI Display devices (Interrupt Management registry keys); the driver default is restored from the snapshot

*Evidence notes:* Applied only to Display devices whose driver created MessageSignaledInterruptProperties.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Revert restores the exact interrupt values the driver had; there is no separate Windows default.

### Accessibility shortcut keys off

*Stops the Sticky/Filter/Toggle Keys pop-ups from 5x Shift, holding Shift or holding Num Lock mid-match.*

If you use these features, they keep working; only the keyboard shortcut that turns them on is disabled. Applied immediately.
