```md
### Enhance pointer precision off

`input.pointer-precision-off` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security 0

*Turns off Windows mouse acceleration so cursor movement matches hand movement 1:1. Applied immediately.*

Sets MouseSpeed, MouseThreshold1 and MouseThreshold2 to "0" (REG_SZ), which is what unticking 'Enhance pointer precision' does, then applies it to the running session through SystemParametersInfo(SPI_SETMOUSE). Most competitive games use raw input, but menus, the desktop and some games use the Windows cursor. Values written with the wrong type by other tools (DWORD) are corrected to REG_SZ.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKCU:\Control Panel\Mouse\MouseSpeed` = `0` (String); Windows default `1`; absent means `1`
- Registry `HKCU:\Control Panel\Mouse\MouseThreshold1` = `0` (String); Windows default `6`; absent means `6`
- Registry `HKCU:\Control Panel\Mouse\MouseThreshold2` = `0` (String); Windows default `10`; absent means `10`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-systemparametersinfow>

*Evidence notes:* SPI_SETMOUSE takes the two thresholds and the acceleration flag; Windows stores them as REG_SZ.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKCU:\Control Panel\Mouse\MouseSpeed: 1. Windows default for HKCU:\Control Panel\Mouse\MouseThreshold1: 6. Windows default for HKCU:\Control Panel\Mouse\MouseThreshold2: 10.

### Fastest key repeat

`input.fast-key-repeat` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security 0

*Shortest repeat delay and fastest repeat rate for held keys. A preference, not a performance change. Applied immediately.*

Sets KeyboardDelay to "0" (about 250 ms) and KeyboardSpeed to "31" (about 30 repeats per second), then applies them through SystemParametersInfo. Games that read raw keyboard input ignore these values; they affect typing, chat and menus.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKCU:\Control Panel\Keyboard\KeyboardDelay` = `0` (String); Windows default `1`; absent means `1`
- Registry `HKCU:\Control Panel\Keyboard\KeyboardSpeed` = `31` (String); Windows default `31`; absent means `31`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-systemparametersinfow>

*Evidence notes:* SPI_SETKEYBOARDDELAY (0-3) and SPI_SETKEYBOARDSPEED (0-31).

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKCU:\Control Panel\Keyboard\KeyboardDelay: 1. Windows default for HKCU:\Control Panel\Keyboard\KeyboardSpeed: 31.

### Network adapter power saving off

`net.adapter-power-saving-off` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency low, security 0

*Unticks 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' on the wired adapter. Legacy setting; measure. Reboot.*

Writes PnPCapabilities = 24 in the active wired adapter's driver key, the value behind the Device Manager option 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'. Prevents Windows from powering the NIC down. Only the active physical Ethernet adapter is touched; virtual and VPN adapters are skipped. Drivers based on NetAdapterCx may ignore this value; check the Device Manager Power Management tab and measure for link drops after resume.

**Changes**

- Active wired adapter driver key `PnPCapabilities` = `24` ("allow the computer to turn off this device" cleared); default `0`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/2848292/power-management-allow-the-computer-to-turn-off-th>

*Evidence notes:* Microsoft KB 2740020 (Windows 7 era) documented PnPCapabilities 24 (0x18) to clear the option and 0 to restore it; that article has been retired, and newer NetAdapterCx drivers may ignore the value, so it is Tier B.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist).

### Energy Efficient Ethernet off

`net.eee-off` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency low, security 0

*Disables EEE (802.3az) low-power idle on the wired adapter, avoiding wake-up latency and link drops.*

Sets the adapter property *EEE to 0 (vendor variants such as 'Green Ethernet' are used only if the driver exposes no *EEE). EEE lets the link enter low-power idle between bursts; Intel documents that the transition adds latency and recommends disabling EEE when it causes speed or drop issues. Written without restarting the adapter; takes effect after an adapter restart or reboot.

**Changes**

- Adapter advanced property `*EEE` = `0` (no adapter restart); fallback only if the keyword is missing: 'Energy Efficient Ethernet' = 'Disabled', 'Energy-Efficient Ethernet' = 'Disabled', 'Green Ethernet' = 'Disabled', 'Advanced EEE' = 'Disabled'; default `1`

**Sources**

- <https://edc.intel.com/content/www/us/en/design/products/ethernet/adapters-and-devices-user-guide/other-power-options>
- <https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000093989/ethernet-products.html>

*Evidence notes:* Vendor documentation (Intel). Marvell AQtion exposes *EEE.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist).

### Receive Side Scaling on

`net.rss-on` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance low, latency low, security 0

*Ensures RSS spreads network receive processing across CPU cores. Usually already on (verify-only).*

Sets *RSS to 1 if a driver or tool turned it off. RSS distributes receive interrupts and DPCs over multiple cores, avoiding one core becoming a bottleneck. It is the Windows and vendor default for modern NICs.

**Changes**

- Adapter advanced property `*RSS` = `1` (no adapter restart); fallback only if the keyword is missing: '' = ''; default `1`

**Sources**

*Evidence notes:* Standardized keyword *RSS.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist).

### TCP auto-tuning: Normal

### Interrupt moderation off

`net.interrupt-moderation-off` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency low, security 0

*NIC interrupts fire per packet instead of being batched: lower latency, more CPU/DPC load. Measure with LatencyMon.*

Sets *InterruptModeration to 0. Moderation batches interrupts to save CPU; turning it off delivers packets to the stack sooner at the cost of more interrupts and DPC time. Game traffic is small, so the latency gain is microseconds; check DPC latency with LatencyMon and measure ping/jitter before and after.

**Changes**

- Adapter advanced property `*InterruptModeration` = `0` (no adapter restart); fallback only if the keyword is missing: '' = ''; default `1`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/network/enumeration-keywords>
- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/network/interrupt-moderation>
- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/technologies/network-subsystem/net-sub-performance-tuning-nics>

*Evidence notes:* Trade-off documented by Microsoft (latency vs CPU utilization).

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist).

### Game traffic QoS marking (DSCP 46)

`net.qos-dscp-games` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency low, security 0

*Marks game UDP packets as Expedited Forwarding. Helps only if your router honors DSCP. Measure ping under load.*

Creates policy-based QoS rules 'iGWindowsTuner-<game>' that tag UDP traffic of the games in games.json with DSCP 46, and sets the Tcpip\QoS 'Do not use NLA' value so the policies also apply on a non-domain PC. A router with QoS/SQM that trusts DSCP can then prioritize game packets. Many consumer routers and ISPs ignore or strip DSCP; measure ping under load (bufferbloat test) before and after.

**Changes**

- Policy-based QoS `iGWindowsTuner-<game>`: DSCP `46` for `UDP` traffic of games marked qos in games.json
- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\QoS\Do not use NLA` = `1` (String); Windows default `<absent>`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/netqos/new-netqospolicy>
- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/technologies/qos/qos-policy-top>

*Evidence notes:* 'Do not use NLA' is documented by router/VoIP vendors (Cisco) rather than Microsoft; it is reversible and harmless if unused.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\QoS\Do not use NLA: <absent>.

### TCP delayed ACK off (TCP games only)

`net.delayed-ack-off` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency low, security 0

*ACKs every TCP segment immediately. No effect on Dota 2, CS2 or VALORANT (UDP). Measure before/after.*

Sets TcpAckFrequency = 1 on the active wired interface so TCP acknowledges every segment instead of waiting up to 200 ms. Can help older TCP-based games and chat clients; UDP games (Dota 2, CS2, VALORANT, LoL) are unaffected. The popular 'TCPNoDelay' interface value is not implemented because Windows TCP does not read it (Nagle is a per-socket option). Measure before/after.

**Changes**

- Registry (active wired adapter) `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces\{InterfaceGuid}\TcpAckFrequency` = `1` (DWord); default `<absent>`

**Sources**

- <https://support.microsoft.com/kb/328890>

*Evidence notes:* Documented by Microsoft (KB 328890).

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist).

### Memory integrity (HVCI) and VBS on

`sec.hvci-on` | Advanced | Tier A | risk medium | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security +

*Keeps virtualization-based security and memory integrity on. Required by FACEIT AC and Vanguard On-Demand. Reboot.*

Sets EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity = 1 and HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity Enabled = 1 without UEFI lock (Microsoft's recommended registry configuration), and confirms through Win32_DeviceGuard that memory integrity is actually running. Raptor Lake supports MBEC, so the performance cost is small. Check Windows Security > Core isolation for incompatible drivers before enabling it for the first time.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity` = `1` (DWord); Windows default `1`
- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\Scenarios\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity\Enabled` = `1` (DWord); Windows default `1`
- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\Scenarios\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity\WasEnabledBy` = `2` (DWord); Windows default `<absent>`; only written when missing
- Verifies at runtime: `HvciRunning` (Win32_DeviceGuard)

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/enable-virtualization-based-protection-of-code-integrity>

*Evidence notes:* Memory integrity is on by default on compatible clean installs of Windows 11, so the documented default used by 'Reset to Windows default' is on.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity: 1. Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\Scenarios\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity\Enabled: 1. Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\Scenarios\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity\WasEnabledBy: <absent>.

### Turn VBS and memory integrity OFF (expert, breaks anti-cheat)

`sec.vbs-hvci-off-expert` | Lab | Tier B | risk high | restart: reboot | Breaks FACEIT, Riot Vanguard | reversible: full | impact: performance low, latency none, security -

> **Warning:** This lowers security and BREAKS FACEIT Anti-Cheat (VBS/IOMMU requirement) and Riot Vanguard On-Demand mode (VBS + HVCI requirement). Keep it off unless you only play games without these anti-cheats.

*EXPERT: disables VBS/HVCI for a few % FPS on some systems. Breaks FACEIT AC and Vanguard On-Demand. Measure first.*

Sets HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity Enabled = 0 and EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity = 0. Microsoft notes memory integrity can cost performance, mostly on CPUs without MBEC; on a 13700K the cost is small. This removes kernel exploit protection, and FACEIT Anti-Cheat and Riot Vanguard On-Demand mode require VBS/HVCI, so those games will refuse to run. Never part of a preset. Measure before deciding.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\Scenarios\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity\Enabled` = `0` (DWord); Windows default `1`
- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity` = `0` (DWord); Windows default `1`
- Verifies at runtime: `HvciNotRunning` (Win32_DeviceGuard)

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/enable-virtualization-based-protection-of-code-integrity>

*Evidence notes:* Security-reducing; offered only as a warned expert toggle as required by the project specification.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\Scenarios\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity\Enabled: 1. Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard\EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity: 1.

### LSA protection (RunAsPPL, no UEFI lock)

`sec.lsa-protection` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security +

*Runs LSASS as a protected process so malware cannot dump credentials. Uses value 2 (no UEFI lock), so it stays reversible.*

Sets RunAsPPL = 2. LSASS runs as a Protected Process Light; non-protected code cannot read its memory or inject into it. Value 2 does not write a UEFI variable, so the setting can be reverted from Windows. An existing value of 1 (with UEFI lock) is respected and left alone.

*Evidence notes:* Value 2 is enforced on Windows 11 22H2 and later.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RunAsPPL: <absent>.

### NTLMv2 only (refuse LM and NTLMv1)

`sec.ntlmv2-only` | Advanced | Tier A | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security +

*Sends only NTLMv2 and refuses old LM/NTLMv1 sign-ins to this PC. Very old NAS boxes or printers that need NTLMv1 may stop working.*

Sets 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' to 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM' (LmCompatibilityLevel = 5). Windows 11 already sends NTLMv2; this also makes the PC refuse the weak LM and NTLMv1 protocols for incoming connections, as the DISA Windows 11 STIG requires. Devices from the SMB1 era that only speak NTLMv1 can no longer connect.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\LmCompatibilityLevel` = `5` (DWord); Windows default `<absent>`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/security-policy-settings/network-security-lan-manager-authentication-level>
- <https://www.stigviewer.com/stigs/microsoft_windows_11_v2r7/2026-02-12/finding/V-253462>

*Evidence notes:* Not defined on clients by default (behaves as 'Send NTLMv2 response only', level 3).

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\LmCompatibilityLevel: <absent>.

### Microsoft vulnerable driver blocklist on

`sec.vulnerable-driver-blocklist` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security +

*Blocks known-vulnerable signed drivers that attackers (and some cheats) abuse to reach the kernel. Windows 11 default.*

Ensures VulnerableDriverBlocklistEnable = 1. Windows refuses to load drivers on Microsoft's vulnerable driver blocklist. On by default in Windows 11; some old RGB or monitoring tools that ship vulnerable drivers (for example WinRing0-based ones) will be blocked.

### WDigest plain-text credential caching off

`sec.wdigest-off` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: logoff | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security +

*Keeps Windows from caching sign-in passwords in clear text for the legacy WDigest protocol. Off by default; repairs it if enabled.*

Ensures UseLogonCredential is 0 (missing also means 0 on Windows 8.1 and later). When a tool or malware sets it to 1, LSASS keeps your password in clear text for WDigest, which credential dumpers read. Nothing is written on a default system. Sign out and back in after a repair to clear cached credentials.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest\UseLogonCredential` = `0` (DWord); Windows default `<absent>`; absent means `0`

### PowerShell script block logging

`sec.ps-scriptblock-logging` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security +

*Records the content of PowerShell scripts in the event log for forensics. Overhead is negligible (measure if you script heavily).*

Sets the EnableScriptBlockLogging policy to 1. PowerShell writes executed script blocks to Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational (event 4104), which makes malicious scripts visible after the fact. Logs can contain secrets typed into scripts. Overhead is negligible for normal use; measure if you run heavy automation.

### Exploit protection system defaults on (DEP, SEHOP, CFG, ASLR)

`sec.exploit-protection-defaults` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security +

*Repairs the system-wide exploit protection defaults (DEP, SEHOP, CFG, bottom-up and high-entropy ASLR) if a tool turned one off.*

Checks the five system-wide exploit protection settings that Windows turns on by default. 'Use default (On)' already counts as on, so nothing is written on a healthy system; a setting that was switched off is set back to On. Mandatory ASLR stays at its Windows default (off) because it can break older programs. Restart after a repair.

**Changes**

- System-wide exploit protection `SEHOP` = ON; default not set
- System-wide exploit protection `CFG` = ON; default not set
- System-wide exploit protection `BottomUp` = ON; default not set
- System-wide exploit protection `HighEntropy` = ON; default not set

Windows default for exploit protection DEP: not set (system default). Windows default for exploit protection SEHOP: not set (system default). Windows default for exploit protection CFG: not set (system default). Windows default for exploit protection BottomUp: not set (system default). ### Block internet access for script and download tools (mshta, wscript, cscript, regsvr32, certutil)

`sec.lolbin-outbound-block` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security +

*Outbound firewall blocks for 5 built-in tools malware abuses to download payloads. Games are unaffected; measure for your own scripts.*

Creates iGWindowsTuner-owned outbound Block rules for mshta, wscript, cscript, regsvr32 and certutil (64-bit and 32-bit copies). Attackers use these signed Windows tools to fetch and run payloads (MITRE ATT&CK T1218, T1105). Windows does not need them to reach the internet, and the rules only stop their own network traffic. Your scripts that download with these tools will fail; measure before relying on them. Reverting removes the rules.

- Windows Firewall block rule `iGWindowsTuner-Block-Out-regsvr32-x64` (Outbound) in group iG Windows Tuner; revert removes it

- Windows Firewall block rule `iGWindowsTuner-Block-Out-certutil-x64` (Outbound) in group iG Windows Tuner; revert removes it

**Sources**

### Windows Script Host off (.vbs, .js, .wsf)

`sec.wsh-off` | Advanced | Tier B | risk medium | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security +

**Side effects:** Programs that rely on .vbs or .js scripts (some old installers, vendor utilities, logon scripts) stop working until the item is turned off.

*Stops wscript and cscript from running .vbs, .js and .wsf files, a common malware launcher. Measure: some old installers need it.*

Sets Windows Script Host 'Enabled' = 0 for the machine. Double-clicked or emailed VBScript and JScript files then refuse to run with 'Windows Script Host access is disabled'. PowerShell, batch files and MSI installers are not affected. Some old installers, login scripts and vendor tools still use WSH; if one breaks, turn this item off again and measure which tool needed it.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Script Host\Settings\Enabled` = `0` (DWord); Windows default `<absent>`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-au/previous-versions/tn-archive/ee198684(v=technet.10)>
- <https://www.cisa.gov/eviction-strategies-tool/info-countermeasures/CM0078>

*Evidence notes:* Microsoft's documentation of the value is archived; CISA lists it as a countermeasure and warns that a few systems' update or recovery tools may use WSH.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Script Host\Settings\Enabled: <absent>.

| Id | Name | Level | Tier | Risk | Restart | Presets | Anti-cheat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `system.pagefile-auto` | Page file managed by Windows | Standard | A | low | reboot | - | safe |
| `system.bsod-details` | Show stop code parameters on the blue screen | Advanced | B | low | reboot | - | safe |

| `system.verbose-status` | Detailed startup, shutdown and sign-in status messages | Advanced | A | low | none | - | safe |

### Page file managed by Windows

`system.pagefile-auto` | Standard | Tier A | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security 0

*Lets Windows size the page file on every drive. Repairs a disabled or too small page file left by tweak tools. Reboot.*

Sets PagingFiles to '?:\pagefile.sys', the system-managed configuration Windows ships with. The page file backs crash dumps and extends the commit limit; a missing or tiny one causes out-of-memory errors and lost crash dumps. Windows grows a system-managed page file only when commit pressure needs it. Turning the item off restores your previous page file setting exactly.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management\PagingFiles` = `?:\pagefile.sys` (MultiString); Windows default `?:\pagefile.sys`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/performance/introduction-to-the-page-file>
- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/performance/memory-dump-file-options>

*Evidence notes:* Windows default: system-managed on all drives.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management\PagingFiles: ?:\pagefile.sys.

### Show stop code parameters on the blue screen

`system.bsod-details` | Advanced | Tier B | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security 0

*Adds the stop code parameters to the blue screen so you can note them before Windows restarts. Undocumented value (Tier B).*

Sets CrashControl DisplayParameters = 1, which adds the four stop code parameters to the blue screen. Microsoft does not document this value; it is widely used and listed in WinUtil, so it is Tier B. There is nothing to measure: it only changes what the stop screen shows, and the minidump records the same parameters.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl\DisplayParameters` = `1` (DWord); Windows default `<absent>`

**Sources**

- <https://winutil.christitus.com/dev/tweaks/customize-preferences/detailedbsod/>

*Evidence notes:* Community-known value; not on Microsoft Learn.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl\DisplayParameters: <absent>.

### Small memory dumps (minidumps) after a crash

`system.dump-small` | Advanced | Tier A | risk low | restart: reboot | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security 0

*Writes a small minidump instead of a memory dump that can be as large as your RAM. Enough to identify the faulting driver. Reboot.*

Sets CrashDumpEnabled to 3 (small memory dump) instead of 7 (automatic memory dump, the Windows default). Each stop error keeps a minidump in %SystemRoot%\Minidump with the stop code, loaded drivers and the faulting thread, which is usually enough to find a bad driver, and no multi-gigabyte MEMORY.DMP is written. Deep kernel debugging needs the automatic dump; turn the item off to get it back.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl\CrashDumpEnabled` = `3` (DWord); Windows default `7`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/performance/memory-dump-file-options>

*Evidence notes:* 0 none, 1 complete, 2 kernel, 3 small, 7 automatic (default).

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl\CrashDumpEnabled: 7.

### Detailed startup, shutdown and sign-in status messages

`system.verbose-status` | Advanced | Tier A | risk low | restart: none | Anti-cheat safe | reversible: full | impact: performance none, latency none, security 0

*Shows what Windows is doing during startup, shutdown and sign-in, which helps find what makes them slow.*

Enables the 'Display highly detailed status messages' policy (VerboseStatus = 1). Instead of 'Please wait', Windows names the step it is on (for example applying policies or stopping a service), so a slow boot or shutdown points to its cause. It has no effect when status messages are turned off by policy.

**Changes**

- Registry `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\VerboseStatus` = `1` (DWord); Windows default `<absent>`

**Sources**

- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/performance/enable-verbose-startup-shutdown-logon-logoff-status-messages>
- <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/ms813386(v=msdn.10)>

*Evidence notes:* Policy value absent by default.

**Revert:** Revert restores the exact values captured in the JSON snapshot taken right before apply (including values that did not exist). Windows default for HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\VerboseStatus: <absent>.
```

`iGWindowsTuner.ps1`:

```ps1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    iG Windows Tuner - auditable Windows 11 gaming performance and security toolbox.

.DESCRIPTION
    Tunes Windows 11 Pro for competitive online gaming while keeping or raising security and
    staying compatible with kernel anti-cheat. Every change is declared in data\tweaks\*.json,
    shown before it is applied, snapshotted to %ProgramData%\iGWindowsTuner\Backups and reversible.

    Without parameters the WPF GUI starts. Read-only modes (-Report, -ListTweaks, -DryRun) never
    change anything and do not need elevation. Modes that change the system relaunch through the
    normal UAC prompt when needed.

.PARAMETER Report
    Read-only health and anti-cheat readiness report.
.PARAMETER ReportPath
    With -Report: also write the report to this .html or .json file.
.PARAMETER ListTweaks
    List every tweak with tier, risk, presets and current state.
.PARAMETER Preset
    Apply a preset: Competitive, Balanced or Hardened.
.PARAMETER Apply
    Apply the given tweak ids.
.PARAMETER Revert
    Revert the given tweak ids from their most recent apply.
.PARAMETER RevertAll
    Revert every tweak of the most recent apply, or of -Snapshot.
.PARAMETER Snapshot
    Snapshot file for -RevertAll.
.PARAMETER ResetDefault
    Reset the given tweak ids to the documented Windows defaults.
.PARAMETER DryRun
    Show exactly what would change and change nothing.
.PARAMETER NoGui
    Never start the GUI (prints help when no mode is given).
.PARAMETER SkipRestorePoint
    Do not create a System Restore point (the JSON snapshot is always written).
.PARAMETER EnableSystemProtection
    Consent to turn on System Protection for the system drive if a restore point cannot be created.
.PARAMETER AcknowledgeRisk
    Required to apply expert toggles (for example turning VBS/HVCI off).
.PARAMETER Json
    Machine-readable output for -Report, -ListTweaks, -DryRun, -Clean and -Analyze.
.PARAMETER Hardware
    Read-only hardware profile: detected hardware tags, the facts behind them and the hardware
    overlays that adjust presets on this PC. With -Json it prints the facts (usable as a test fixture).
.PARAMETER Clean
    Cleaning engine. With -Scan (or -DryRun) it only enumerates and sizes (read-only). Without it,
    it scans, shows the result and deletes only what the scan found after you type YES (or -Yes).
.PARAMETER Scan
    With -Clean: scan only; nothing is deleted.
.PARAMETER CleanRule
    With -Clean: rule ids to use (default: the rules that are on by default up to -CleanLevel).
.PARAMETER CleanLevel
    With -Clean: highest rule level to include (Standard, Advanced, Expert).
.PARAMETER IncludeOptIn
    With -Clean: include rules that are off by default.
.PARAMETER AllUsers
    With -Clean: expand per-user rules to every local profile (requires administrator rights).
.PARAMETER Yes
    With -Clean: skip the YES confirmation (needed with -Json).
.PARAMETER Analyze
    Read-only disk analyzer: largest folders and files under this folder or drive.
.PARAMETER Top
    With -Analyze: number of folders and files to list.
.PARAMETER Asr
    ASR Center. Alone it lists every attack surface reduction rule with its mode, recommendation,
    gamer impact and exclusions (read-only). With -AsrMode, -AsrRecommended, -AsrExclude or
    -AsrUnexclude it changes rules or exclusions after writing a snapshot (-DryRun shows the plan).
.PARAMETER AsrRule
    With -Asr: the rule (key such as 'psexec-wmi' or GUID) to show, set or exclude for.
.PARAMETER AsrMode
    With -Asr -AsrRule: NotConfigured, Audit, Warn or Block.
.PARAMETER AsrRecommended
    With -Asr: raise every rule that is below its recommended mode (never lowers a rule).
.PARAMETER AsrExclude
    With -Asr: paths to exclude. With -AsrRule only from that rule, otherwise from all ASR rules.
    Separate several paths with '|'.
.PARAMETER AsrUnexclude
    With -Asr: paths to remove from the same exclusion list.
.PARAMETER AsrAudit
    Read-only ASR audit view: ASR, controlled folder access and network protection events grouped
    by rule and program, with recommendations.
.PARAMETER Days
    With -AsrAudit: how many days of events to read (1-90, default 14).
.PARAMETER SecurityScore
    Read-only security score with the fix for every failed check, plus the local accounts audit.
.PARAMETER NetworkSurface
    Read-only listening-ports report: programs that accept connections and on which interfaces.
.PARAMETER Inspect
    Read-only expert inspectors: All, Power (processor power settings of the active plan, hidden
    ones included), Interrupts (PCI interrupt modes and affinity), Network (RSS, queues, buffers),
    Kernel (kernel and memory registry values with Windows defaults), Timer, Crash (dumps, page file).
.PARAMETER PowerSetting
    Power plan editor (Expert): the processor setting to change, by alias (for example PERFEPP).
    Use with -Ac, -Dc or -PowerDefault, and -AcknowledgeRisk. -DryRun validates and shows the change.
.PARAMETER Ac
    With -PowerSetting: new plugged-in value.
.PARAMETER Dc
    With -PowerSetting: new battery value.
.PARAMETER PowerDefault
    With -PowerSetting: return the setting to the Windows default of the plan.
.PARAMETER Inventory
    Read-only management views: Services (with the safe-to-change rating), Tasks, Apps, Features
    (administrator), Firewall (rule browser), Hosts (hosts-file viewer), Adapters (every advanced
    property with a description). Filter rows with -Search.
.PARAMETER Search
    With -Inventory: show only rows whose name, display name, path or program contains this text.
.PARAMETER Change
    Snapshot-backed management change: service, task, appx, feature, capability or firewallRule.
    Needs -Target and -Value; protected targets are refused. -DryRun validates and shows the change.
.PARAMETER Target
    With -Change: service name, full task path, package name, feature, capability or firewall rule name.
.PARAMETER Value
    With -Change: service Automatic/AutomaticDelayed/Manual/Disabled; task, feature and firewall rule
    Enabled/Disabled; appx Removed; capability Installed/NotPresent.
.PARAMETER Provisioned
    With -Change appx: also remove the provisioned copy (new user profiles do not get the app).
.PARAMETER Persistence
    Read-only Persistence Inspector (Autoruns-style) with signature status. -ReportPath exports it
    (.html or .json); -IncludeMicrosoft also lists Microsoft-signed services, drivers and tasks.
.PARAMETER IncludeMicrosoft
    With -Persistence: include Microsoft-signed entries (slower).
.PARAMETER Updates
    Read-only Windows Update status: services, pending restart, Windows Update for Business policies, history.
.PARAMETER Diagnostics
    Read-only diagnostics: All, DpcIsr, Reliability, Crashes, Boot, Drivers. -Days sets the history window.
.PARAMETER SystemReport
    Full read-only system report written to -ReportPath (.html or .json). -Quick skips the slow sections.
.PARAMETER Quick
    With -SystemReport: skip persistence signatures and DPC sampling.
.PARAMETER DnsBenchmark
    User-initiated DNS benchmark of the current DNS servers and public resolvers (uses the network, changes nothing).
.PARAMETER Latency
    User-initiated latency, jitter and loss test to the host names or IP addresses you give.

.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Report
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Preset Competitive -DryRun
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Apply input.pointer-precision-off,gfx.game-mode
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -RevertAll
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Clean -Scan -CleanLevel Advanced -IncludeOptIn
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Clean -CleanRule clean.user.temp,clean.gaming.nvidia-shader
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Analyze C:\ -Top 30
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Asr -AsrRecommended -DryRun
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Asr -AsrRule copied-system-tools -AsrExclude "D:\Games\MyGame\MyGame.exe"
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -AsrAudit -Days 30
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Inspect Power,Interrupts
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -PowerSetting PERFEPP -Ac 20 -AcknowledgeRisk -DryRun
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Inventory Services -Search xbox
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Change service -Target XblGameSave -Value Manual -DryRun
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Persistence -ReportPath "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\persistence.html"
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Diagnostics Crashes,Drivers -Days 60
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -SystemReport -ReportPath "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\system-report.html"
.EXAMPLE
    .\iGWindowsTuner.ps1 -Latency 1.1.1.1,valve.net

.NOTES
    Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error, 2 invalid arguments or unknown tweak/rule id, 3 elevation declined,
    4 preflight refused (unsupported build, System Protection off), 5 one or more tweaks or cleaner
    rules failed, 6 nothing to revert, 3010 success and a reboot is required.
#>
```
